subPoints.heading: Basketball game
subPoints.body: Basketball is played by 2 teams of 5 players each. The aim of each team is to score in the opponents’ basket and to prevent the other team from scoring. The game is conducted by the referees, table officials and a commissioner (including technical delegate), if present.

subPoints.heading: Participants’ responsibility
subPoints.body: All participants, table officials, commissioners, players, coaches and accompanying delegation members must uphold ethical behaviour and notify the referees immediately if they become aware of a correctable inaccuracy involving the score, fouls, time-outs, or clock/shot-clock operations.

subPoints.heading: Basket: opponents’ / own
subPoints.body: The basket attacked by a team is the opponents’ basket, and the basket defended by a team is its own basket.

subPoints.heading: Winner of a game
subPoints.body: The team that has scored the greater number of points at the end of playing time shall be the winner.

examples.text: During Q1 a 3-point shot by A1 is erroneously entered on the scoreboard as 2 points. Participants notice the inaccuracy (see OBRI F-3.3.26).
examples.interpretation: Under Art. 1.2, players/coaches/table officials are expected to notify referees immediately so correctable errors (Art. 45 / IRS) can be fixed within rule limits.

subPoints.heading: Court dimensions
subPoints.body: Flat, hard, obstruction-free playing surface measuring 28 m in length by 15 m in width from the inner edge of the boundary line.

subPoints.heading: Floor
subPoints.body: Includes the court surrounded by a further boundary lane free from obstructions of at least 2 m in width (minimum floor size 32 m × 19 m).

subPoints.heading: Backcourt
subPoints.body: Consists of the team’s own basket, the inbounds part of the backboard, and the court area limited by the endline behind its own basket, sidelines, and centre line.

subPoints.heading: Frontcourt
subPoints.body: Consists of the opponents’ basket, the inbounds part of the backboard, and the court area limited by the endline behind the opponents’ basket, sidelines, and inner edge of the centre line nearest the opponents’ basket.

subPoints.heading: Lines (overview)
subPoints.body: All lines are solid colour, 5 cm wide, in high contrast. Boundary, throw-in and bench lines must share one colour; matching pairs on each half-court (restricted areas, FT semi-circles, 3-point lines, no-charge semi-circles) must match.

subPoints.heading: Boundary line
subPoints.body: Endlines and sidelines limit the court and are NOT part of the court. All bench personnel and obstructions must be at least 2 m from the court.

subPoints.heading: Centre line, centre circle and free-throw semi-circles
subPoints.body: Centre line extends 0.15 m beyond each sideline and is part of the backcourt. Centre circle and free-throw semi-circles have a 1.80 m outer radius.

subPoints.heading: Free-throw lines, restricted areas and rebound places
subPoints.body: Free-throw line furthest edge is 5.80 m from inner endline (3.60 m long). Restricted areas extend 2.45 m from mid-point on either side; markings are part of the restricted area.

subPoints.heading: 3-point goal area
subPoints.body: Parallel lines 0.90 m from inner edge of sidelines joined to a 6.75 m arc measured from beneath the centre of the basket (1.575 m from endline). The 3-point line is NOT part of the 3-point goal area.

subPoints.heading: Team bench areas
subPoints.body: Must provide 16 seats for head coach, substitutes, excluded players, and accompanying delegation members; others must sit at least 2 m behind.

subPoints.heading: Throw-in lines
subPoints.body: 4 lines (2 per sideline), 0.15 m long outside the court, outer edge 8.325 m from the inner edge of the nearest endline.

subPoints.heading: No-charge semi-circle areas (2026: 1.30 m radius)
subPoints.body: Semi-circle with 1.30 m outer radius beneath exact centre of basket joined to 2 parallel lines 0.375 m long ending 1.20 m from inner endline. The semi-circle lines ARE part of the no-charge semi-circle areas.

subPoints.heading: Scorer’s table and substitution chairs
subPoints.body: Must be placed on a platform in the order: Shot clock operator (1), Timer (2), Commissioner (3), Scorer (4), Assistant scorer (5), flanked by substitution chairs.

examples.text: The colours of the boundary lines and other court markings may differ. The colour of each pair of other court markings must match on both half-courts. The centre line and the centre circle may be of a different colour than the boundary lines and other court markings.
The sidelines and the endlines are white, the 3-point lines and the free-throw semi-circles are green.
examples.interpretation: These court markings are permitted. All boundary lines, including sidelines and endlines must be of the same colour. The colour of each pair of the 3-point lines and free-throw semi-circles on both half-courts may differ from the colour of the sidelines and the endlines.

examples.text: The centre line is orange and the centre circle line is blue.
examples.interpretation: These court markings are permitted. The centre line and the centre circle, between each other, may be of different colours.

examples.text: The sidelines, endlines, throw-in lines and team bench area lines are black. The restricted areas and free-throw lines are red on both half-courts. The centre line is white and the centre circle is green. All markings are clearly visible.
examples.interpretation: These court markings are permitted. The boundary lines are of the same colour, the paired markings match on both half-courts, and the centre line and centre circle may be of different colours.

examples.text: One 3-point line is blue and the 3-point line on the opposite half-court is white.
examples.interpretation: This is not permitted. The colour of each pair of court markings must match on both half-courts.

subPoints.heading: Required arena and table equipment
subPoints.body: Required equipment for every official FIBA game:
bullets: Backstop units: backboards, pressure-release rings and nets, padded support structures.
Basketballs, game clock, scoreboard, shot clock, and separate timeout stopwatch.
2 distinctly different loud signals (one for timer, one for shot clock operator).
Official scoresheet, player/head coach foul markers (1–5 + GD), team foul markers, alternating possession arrow.
Compliant floor, court markings, and adequate lighting.

examples.text: The shot clock horn and game clock horn must use two distinctly different loud sounds, and time-outs must be timed with a separate stopwatch (not the game clock).
examples.interpretation: Crew chief verifies all required arena equipment before tip-off under Art. 47.1.

subPoints.heading: Definition (4.1.1 – 4.1.4)
subPoints.body: A team member is eligible if authorised by the competition and entitled to play when entered on the scoresheet before start of game (unless disqualified or at 5 fouls).
bullets: 4.1.1 Eligible under organising body regulations (including age limits).
4.1.2 Entitled to play once on scoresheet, not disqualified, < 5 fouls.
4.1.3 During playing time: player (on court), substitute (off court), or excluded player (5 fouls).
4.1.4 During intervals of play, all team members entitled to play are considered players.

subPoints.heading: Team composition (4.2.1 – 4.2.3)
subPoints.body: Maximum 12 entitled team members (including captain), 1 head coach, and up to 8 accompanying delegation members (first assistant coach must be on scoresheet). 5 players on court during playing time.

subPoints.heading: Uniforms (4.3.1 – 4.3.3)
subPoints.body: Shirts and shorts of same dominant colour front/back (sleeves above elbow; shirts tucked in; all-in-ones permitted; socks same dominant colour).
bullets: 4.3.2 Plain contrasting numbers 0, 00, and 1–99 (back >= 16 cm, front >= 8 cm, width >= 2 cm, >= 4 cm from logos).
4.3.3 Home team wears light-coloured shirts (preferably white); visiting team dark-coloured unless agreed otherwise.

subPoints.heading: Other equipment (4.4.1 – 4.4.5)
subPoints.body: No unfair advantage or injury-causing objects.
bullets: Prohibited: hard finger/hand/wrist/elbow/forearm guards, casts/helmets even if padded, sharp objects, jewellery, hair accessories.

Permitted: padded upper-arm/thigh/leg guards, compression sleeves/shorts, safe headgear not covering face, knee/shoulder/ankle braces, nose protector, transparent mouthguard, safe spectacles, textile wristbands/headbands <= 10 cm. All team compression/headgear/wristbands/tapings must share one solid colour.
4.4.3–4.4.5 Shoes any colour (no flashing lights/reflective adornments); no commercial/promotional body/hair logos.

examples.text: All players on the team must have all their arm and leg compression garments, including undershirts and undershorts, headgear, wristbands, headbands and tapings of the same solid colour.
A1 wears a white headband and A2 wears a red headband on the court.
examples.interpretation: A1 and A2 wearing different colour headbands is not permitted.

examples.text: A1 wears a white headband and A2 wears a red wristband on the court.
examples.interpretation: A1 wearing a white headband and A2 wearing a red wristband is not permitted.

examples.text: Wearing of scarf-style headbands is not permitted (Diagram 1).
A1 wears a scarf-style headband of the same solid colour as any other additional permitted equipment of the team-mates.
examples.interpretation: A1 wearing a scarf-style headband is not permitted. The headband shall not have opening/closing elements around the head and shall not have any parts extruding from its surface.

examples.text: A6 requests a substitution. The referees recognise that A6 wears a non-compression T-shirt under the shirt.
examples.interpretation: The substitution shall not be granted. Only compression garments may be worn under the uniform.

examples.text: A6 wears a compression garment under the shorts extending to (a) above the knees; (b) the ankles.
examples.interpretation: The compression garment (undershorts) is legal and may be worn with any length. All players on the team must have all their compression garments, including undershirts and undershorts, headgear, wristbands, headbands and tapings of the same solid colour.

examples.text: A6 wears a compression garment (undershirt) under the playing shirt extending to (a) the shoulders; (b) the neck.
examples.interpretation: The compression garment (undershirt) is legal and may be worn (a) with any length on and below the shoulders, (b) up to the bottom of the neck. All players on the team must have all their compression garments, headgear, wristbands, headbands and tapings of the same solid colour.

examples.text: The socks of all team members shall be of the same dominant colour. The socks do not have to be visible.
10 team A players wear white socks and 2 players wear black socks.
examples.interpretation: This is not permitted. The socks of all team members shall have the same dominant colour.

examples.text: 7 team A players wear black socks while the socks of other 5 team A players are covered by ankle braces or compression garments, or are otherwise not visible.
examples.interpretation: This is permitted. The socks do not have to be visible.

subPoints.heading: Stopping the game
subPoints.body: In the event of injury to a player(s), the referees may stop the game.

subPoints.heading: Live ball timing for stoppage
subPoints.body: If the ball is live, referees wait until the team in control shoots, loses control, withholds play, or ball becomes dead — unless immediate stoppage is needed to protect an injured player.

subPoints.heading: 15-second / assistance substitution rule
subPoints.body: If an injured player cannot continue immediately (~15 seconds) or receives treatment/assistance from bench personnel, that player MUST be substituted unless the team would be reduced below 5 players.

subPoints.heading: Court entry for treatment / doctor
subPoints.body: Coaches/bench personnel require referee permission to attend an injured player; when the ball is dead, a doctor may enter without permission if immediate medical treatment is required.

subPoints.heading: Bleeding, time-out recovery & starter/FT injuries
subPoints.body: Any bleeding player or open wound must be substituted until stopped and securely covered. Recovering during a time-out before timer’s signal allows remaining in the game (5.7). If a designated starter or FT shooter is substituted for injury before playing/between FTs, opponents may substitute the same number of players (5.8).

examples.text: If a player is injured, appears to be injured or in need of assistance and, as a result, any person permitted to sit on the team bench (head coach, first assistant coach, substitutes, excluded players or accompanying delegation members of the same team) enters the court, that player is considered to have received treatment or assistance, whether or not actual treatment or assistance was performed.

A1 appears to have an injured ankle and the game is stopped. The team A (a) doctor enters the court and treats A1’s injured ankle; (b) doctor enters the court but A1 has already recovered; (c) head coach enters the court to look after the injured player; (d) first assistant coach, substitute, excluded player or any other accompanying delegation member enters the court but does not treat A1.
examples.interpretation: In all cases, A1 received a treatment and shall be substituted.

examples.text: The team’s physiotherapist enters the court and fixes a loose taping on A1.
examples.interpretation: A1 received assistance and shall be substituted.

examples.text: The team’s doctor enters the court to find A1’s lost contact lens.
examples.interpretation: A1 received assistance and shall be substituted.

examples.text: Any person permitted to sit on the team’s bench, while remaining in the team’s bench area, may provide assistance to a player on their own team. If the assistance does not delay the game from being restarted promptly, that player is not considered to have received assistance and shall not be required to be substituted.

B1 fouls A1 in the act of shooting, close to the team A bench area. The ball does not enter the basket. While A1 attempts 2 or 3 free throws: (a) the team A manager or A6 from the team’s bench area passes a towel, a water bottle or a headband to any other team A player on the court; (b) the team A physiotherapist from the team’s bench area fixes a loose taping of any other team A player on the court or sprays the player’s leg or massages the player’s neck, etc.
examples.interpretation: In both cases, the team A player has not received assistance that delays the game from being restarted promptly. The team A player shall not be required to be substituted. A1 shall continue to attempt 2 or 3 free throws.

examples.text: B1 fouls A1 in the act of shooting, close to the team A bench area. The ball does not enter the basket. After the foul, A1 falls on the court and into the team’s bench area. A6 stands up and helps A1 to the feet. A1 is ready to play immediately; at the latest, within approximately 15 seconds.
examples.interpretation: A1 has not received assistance that delays the game from being restarted promptly. A1 shall not be required to be substituted. A1 shall attempt 2 or 3 free throws.

examples.text: A1 is awarded 2 free throws. While the referee communicates the foul at the scorer’s table, A1 goes to a place in front of the team’s bench area at the far end of the court and asks for a towel or a water bottle. Any person from the team’s bench area passes A1 a towel or a water bottle. A1 dries the hands or takes a drink. A1 is ready to play immediately, at the latest, within approximately 15 seconds.
examples.interpretation: A1 has not received assistance that delays the game from being restarted promptly. A1 shall not be required to be substituted. A1 shall attempt 2 free throws.

examples.text: A1 scores a goal. Thrower-in B1 indicates to the referee that the ball is wet. The referee stops the game. Any person from the team B bench area comes on to the court and dries the ball or gives a towel to B1 to dry the ball.
examples.interpretation: In both cases, B1 has not received assistance that delays the game from being restarted promptly. B1 shall not be required to be substituted. The game shall be resumed with a team B throw-in from any place behind the endline, except from directly behind the backboard. The referee shall hand the ball to a team B player for the throw-in.

examples.text: A1 has the ball in the hands for a throw-in from the frontcourt. The team A physiotherapist leaves the team bench area in the backcourt, remains outside the court and fixes the taping of A1.
examples.interpretation: The team A physiotherapist provided assistance to A1 outside of the team bench area. A1 shall be required to be substituted.

examples.text: A1 does not yet have the ball in the hands for a throw-in from the frontcourt. The team A physiotherapist remains in the team bench area in the frontcourt and fixes the taping of A1.
examples.interpretation: The team A physiotherapist provided assistance to A1 within the team bench area. If the assistance is completed within 15 seconds, A1 shall not be required to be substituted. If the assistance lasts more than 15 seconds, A1 shall be required to be substituted.

examples.text: There is no time limit for the removal of a seriously injured player from the court if, according to a doctor’s opinion, the removal is dangerous for the player.
A1 appears to be seriously injured and the game is stopped for about 15 minutes because the doctor believes that removal from the court could be dangerous for the player.
examples.interpretation: The doctor’s opinion shall determine the appropriate time for the removal of the injured player from the court. After the substitution, the game shall be resumed without any penalty.

examples.text: If a player is injured or bleeding or has an open wound and cannot continue to play immediately (within approximately 15 seconds), or if assisted by any person permitted to sit on that team’s bench, the player must be substituted. If a time-out is granted to either team in the same game clock stopped period, and that player recovers or the assistance is completed during the time-out, the player may continue to play only if the timer’s signal for the end of the time-out sounds before a referee beckons a substitute to replace the injured or assisted player.

A1 is injured and the game is stopped. As A1 is not able to continue to play immediately, a referee blows the whistle making the conventional sign for a substitution. Either team requests a time-out (a) before a substitute for A1 enters the game; (b) after a substitute for A1 enters the game. At the end of the time-out, A1 has recovered and requests to remain in the game.
examples.interpretation: (a) If A1 recovers during the time-out, A1 may continue to play. (b) A substitute for A1 has already entered the game, therefore A1 cannot re-enter until the next game clock running period has ended.

examples.text: Players designated by their head coach to start the game may be substituted in case of an injury. Players who receive treatment between free throws must be substituted in case of an injury. In both cases, the opponents are also entitled to substitute the same number of players, if they wish.

A1 is fouled and is awarded 2 free throws. After the first free throw the referees recognise that (a) A1 is bleeding and is substituted by A6 (Team B requests to substitute 2 players); (b) B1 is bleeding and is substituted by B6 (Team A requests to substitute 1 player).
examples.interpretation: In (a) team B is entitled to substitute only 1 player. A6 shall attempt the second free throw. In (b) team A is entitled to substitute 1 player. A1 shall attempt the second free throw.

subPoints.heading: Communication on court
subPoints.body: The captain (CAP) represents the team on court and may courteously obtain information from referees only when the ball is dead and game clock is stopped.

subPoints.heading: Protesting game result
subPoints.body: The captain must inform the crew chief within 15 minutes after the end of the game if the team protests the result and sign the scoresheet in the protest column.

examples.text: Team A believes an Art. 45 error was not corrected despite verifiable evidence and wishes to protest the game result.
examples.interpretation: Under Art. 6.2 & Appendix C, only the captain (CAP) notifies the crew chief within 15 minutes after the game ends and signs the protest column on the scoresheet.

articles.title: Head coach and first assistant coach: Duties and powers

subPoints.heading: Pre-game roster & starting five
subPoints.body: Submit eligible list (>= 40 min before scheduled start); sign scoresheet and designate starting 5 (>= 10 min before start, Team A first).

subPoints.heading: Bench conduct & standing rule
subPoints.body: Only listed personnel remain in bench area; substitutes/excluded players stay seated. Either head coach OR first assistant coach (only one at a time) may stand. Only the head coach may communicate courteously with referees (when clock stopped/ball dead).

subPoints.heading: Succession & FT designation
subPoints.body: First assistant coach assumes head coach powers if head coach cannot continue (7.7). If neither is available, captain acts as player head coach (7.9). Head coach designates free-throw shooter whenever rules do not specify one (7.10).

examples.text: At least 40 minutes before the game is scheduled to start, each team’s head coach or representative shall give the scorer a team list with names and corresponding numbers (indicating captain with CAP), head coach and first assistant coach. At least 10 minutes before the game is scheduled to start, each head coach shall sign the scoresheet confirming the entries.

Team A presents in due time the team list to the scorer. The shirt numbers of 2 players are different than their actual shirt numbers or the name of a player is omitted on the scoresheet. This is recognised (a) before the start of the game; (b) after the start of the game.
examples.interpretation: (a) The wrong numbers shall be corrected, or the name of the player shall be added on the scoresheet without any penalty. (b) The referee stops the game at a convenient time so as not to disadvantage either team. The wrong numbers shall be corrected without any penalty. However, the name of the omitted player cannot be added on the scoresheet.

examples.text: Team A head coach wishes to have injured players or players not intended to play to be permitted to sit on the team bench during the game.
examples.interpretation: The teams are free to decide who of the maximum of 12 team members eligible to play shall be entered on the scoresheet and entitled to sit on the team bench during the game, in addition to a maximum of 8 team accompanying delegation members.

examples.text: At least 10 minutes before the game is scheduled to start, each team’s head coach shall confirm the 5 players who are to start the game. If an error regarding these 5 players is recognised before the start of the game, the starting 5 players shall be corrected. If recognised after the start of the game, the error shall be disregarded.
It is recognised that one of the players on the court is not one of the confirmed starting 5 players. This occurs (a) before the start of the game; (b) after the start of the game.
examples.interpretation: (a) The player shall be replaced by one of the 5 players who were to start the game without any penalty. (b) The error shall be disregarded. The game shall continue without any penalty.

examples.text: The head coach requests the scorer to enter the small “x” on the scoresheet for the 5 players who are to start the game.
examples.interpretation: The head coach shall personally confirm the 5 players who are to start the game by marking a small “x” beside each player’s number in the “Player in” column on the scoresheet.

examples.text: The team A head coach and the team A first assistant coach are disqualified.
examples.interpretation: The team A captain shall act as the team A player head coach.

articles.title: Playing time, tied score and overtime

subPoints.heading: Quarters and intervals
subPoints.body: 4 quarters of 10 minutes; 20 min pre-game interval; 2 min between Q1–Q2, Q3–Q4, and before each overtime; 15 min half-time.

subPoints.heading: Start and end of intervals
subPoints.body: Interval ends on jump-ball release in Q1 or when ball is at thrower-in’s disposal for all other quarters/overtimes.

subPoints.heading: Overtime, 0.1 s minimum & interval fouls
subPoints.body: Tied score at end of Q4 triggers 5-minute overtimes (or tied aggregate in home-and-away series). Minimum 0.1 s shown after end-of-quarter foul (8.8). Technical/flagrant/disqualifying fouls during an interval have free throws shot before the next quarter/overtime starts (8.9).

examples.text: An interval of play starts 20 minutes before the game is scheduled to start, or when the game clock signal sounds for the end of the quarter or any overtime, except the last one. When the backboard is equipped with red lighting around its perimeter, the lighting takes precedence over the game clock signal sound.
B1 is charged with a personal foul committed against A1 in the (a) unsuccessful or (b) successful act of shooting before the game clock signal sounds for the end of the quarter.
examples.interpretation: The referees shall consult immediately and determine whether B1’s foul occurred before the signal sounded. If before: in (a) A1 attempts 2 free throws; in (b) A1’s goal counts and A1 attempts 1 free throw; clock reset to time remaining when foul occurred. If after the signal sounded, the foul is disregarded and the goal, if made, shall not count.

examples.text: A1 attempts a shot for a 3-point goal. The ball is in the air when the game clock signal sounds for the end of the game. After the signal, B1 fouls A1 who is still airborne. The ball enters the basket.
examples.interpretation: A1 shall be awarded 3 points. B1’s foul against A1 shall be disregarded as it occurred after the end of playing time, unless B1’s foul meets the criteria of a flagrant or disqualifying foul and there is a quarter or overtime to follow.

articles.title: Start and end of a quarter, overtime or the game

subPoints.heading: Starting conditions
subPoints.body: Q1 begins when ball leaves crew chief’s hands on centre toss; other quarters/OTs begin at thrower-in’s disposal. Game cannot start unless each team has 5 players ready on court.

subPoints.heading: Benches, basket exchange & red LED precedence
subPoints.body: Home team takes bench left of scorer’s table; teams switch baskets for second half (overtimes stay same as Q4). Backboard perimeter red lighting takes precedence over sound signal (9.7).

examples.text: A game shall not start unless each team has a minimum of 5 players on the court ready to play.
At the start of the second half, team A cannot present 5 players on the court because of injuries, disqualifications etc.
examples.interpretation: The obligation to present a minimum of 5 players is valid only at the start of the game. Team A may continue to play with fewer than 5 players.

examples.text: Close to the end of the game, A1 is charged with a fifth foul and becomes an excluded player. Team A is reduced to 4 players as they have no more substitutes available. As team B is leading by a large margin, the team B head coach demonstrating fair play wants to remove one of the players to also play with 4 players.
examples.interpretation: The request by the team B head coach to play with fewer than 5 players shall be denied. If a team has sufficient players available, 5 players shall be on the court.

examples.text: If by confusion any quarter or overtime starts with both teams attacking/defending the wrong baskets, the situation shall be corrected as soon as it is recognised, without placing either team at a disadvantage. Any points scored, time used, fouls charged, etc. before the stopping of the game remain valid.
After the start of the game, the referees recognise that teams are playing in the wrong direction.
examples.interpretation: The game shall be stopped as soon as possible without placing either team at a disadvantage. Teams shall correct the direction of play. The game shall be resumed from the mirror-opposite place to where the game was stopped.

examples.text: The game shall start with a jump ball at the centre circle.
At the start of the game jumper B1 is charged with a personal foul against A1 (a) before or (b) after the ball has left the hands of the crew chief on the toss for the opening jump ball.
examples.interpretation: (a) First quarter has not yet started (foul during interval); game starts with a jump ball. (b) First quarter has started; resumed with team A throw-in from behind sideline in frontcourt nearest centre line with 14 seconds on shot clock. In both cases, foul counts toward team B Q1 fouls.

examples.text: During the interval of play before the game, A1 is charged with a category 1 technical foul. Before the start of the game, the team B head coach designates B6 to attempt 1 free throw, however B6 is not one of the team B starting 5 players.
examples.interpretation: Only one of the designated team B starting 5 players shall attempt the free throw with no line-up. A substitution cannot be granted before playing time has started. The game shall start with a jump ball.

examples.text: During the interval of play before the game, A1 is charged with a flagrant foul committed against B1.
examples.interpretation: Before the start of the game, B1 shall attempt 2 free throws with no line-up. If B1 is confirmed as one of the 5 players to start the game, B1 shall remain on the court; if not, B1 shall not remain on the court. The game shall start with a jump ball and with the 5 team B players confirmed to start the game.

examples.text: If during an interval of play before the game a player designated as one of the starting 5 players is no longer able or entitled to start the game, that player shall be replaced by another player. In this case, the opponents are entitled to replace one player of its starting 5 players, if they wish.
A1 is one of the team A starting 5 players. During the interval of play 7 minutes before the game (a) A1 becomes injured; (b) A1 is charged with a disqualifying foul.
examples.interpretation: In both cases, A1 shall be replaced with another team A player. Team B is entitled to replace one of its starting 5 players, if they wish.

subPoints.heading: Live ball
subPoints.body: Becomes live on jump-ball toss release, at free-throw shooter’s disposal, or at thrower-in’s disposal.

subPoints.heading: Dead ball
subPoints.body: Becomes dead on made goal/FT, whistle on live ball, apparent missed FT followed by another FT/possession, game clock end signal, shot clock signal while in team control, or touching a shot in flight after whistle/horn.

subPoints.heading: Exceptions (goal still counts)
subPoints.body: Ball in flight on a shot/FT when whistle or horn sounds still counts if made; continuous motion shot started before an opponent/bench foul still finishes legally unless an entirely new act of shooting is made after the whistle.

examples.text: The ball does not become dead and the goal, if made, shall count when a player is in the act of shooting and finishes the shot with a continuous motion while any player of the defensive team is charged with a foul against any opponent after the act of shooting has started. This statement is equally valid if any person permitted to sit on the defensive team bench is charged with a category 1 technical foul.
A1 is in the act of shooting when B2 fouls A2. A1 finishes the shot with a continuous motion. (a) This is the third team B foul in the quarter. (b) This is the fifth team B foul in the quarter.
examples.interpretation: In both cases, A1’s goal, if made, shall count. In (a) the game shall be resumed with a team A throw-in from the place nearest to where B2’s foul occurred. In (b) A2 shall attempt 2 free throws. The game shall be resumed as after any last free throw.

examples.text: A1 is in the act of shooting when A2 fouls B2. A1 finishes the shot with a continuous motion.
examples.interpretation: The ball becomes dead when A2 is charged with a team control foul. If A1’s shot is successful, the goal shall not count. Regardless of the number of team A fouls in the quarter, the game shall be resumed with a team B throw-in from the free-throw line extended (or, if unsuccessful, nearest where foul occurred except behind backboard).

articles.title: Location of a player and a referee

subPoints.heading: Floor contact and airborne status
subPoints.body: Location is where a player or referee touches the floor; while airborne, status (boundary, centre, 3-point, FT, restricted area, no-charge semi-circle lines) is retained from last floor contact. Ball touching a referee equals floor at referee’s location.

examples.text: A1 jumps from inbounds frontcourt, intercepts a pass while airborne, and passes before landing, OR ball hits referee straddling the centre line (see OBRI 30-10).
examples.interpretation: Airborne player retains the status of where they last touched the floor; ball hitting a referee is treated identically to touching the floor at the referee’s location.

subPoints.heading: Jump ball procedure & penalty
subPoints.body: Held ball occurs when opponents firmly hold ball without undue roughness (12.1.2). Jumpers stand inside own half of centre circle; ball must be tapped after downward flight begins; max 2 taps; non-jumpers stay outside circle cylinder until tapped (12.2). Violation awards throw-in to opponents (12.3).

subPoints.heading: Jump ball situations
subPoints.body: Held ball; out-of-bounds doubt/disagreement; double FT violation on missed last FT; live ball lodged between ring/backboard (except between FTs or before frontcourt throw-in penalty); dead ball with neither team entitled; equal foul cancellation; start of Q2, Q3, Q4, and OTs.

subPoints.heading: Alternating possession procedure
subPoints.body: Team not gaining first live-ball control after Q1 jump ball gets first AP throw-in (12.6.2). Arrow reverses immediately when AP throw-in ends, or if violating team commits throw-in violation (losing arrow). A foul before quarter/OT or during AP throw-in does NOT forfeit AP right (12.6.6).

examples.text: The team that does not gain the first team control of a live ball after the opening jump ball at the start of the game shall be awarded the ball for a throw-in from the place nearest to where the next jump ball situation occurs, except from directly behind the backboard.
Two minutes before the start of the game, A1 is charged with a technical foul of any category.
examples.interpretation: One of the 5 team B starting players shall attempt the free throw with no line-up. As the game has not yet started, the direction of the alternating possession arrow cannot be placed in favour of any team yet. The game shall start with a jump ball.

examples.text: The crew chief tosses the ball for the opening jump ball. Before the ball reaches its highest point, jumper A1 touches the ball.
examples.interpretation: This is a jump ball violation by A1. Team B shall be awarded a throw-in from its frontcourt, close to the centre line with 14 seconds on the shot clock. Once at team B’s disposal, team A gets the first alternating possession arrow.

examples.text: The crew chief tosses the ball for the opening jump ball. Before the ball reaches its highest point, non-jumper A2 enters the centre circle from the (a) backcourt; (b) frontcourt.
examples.interpretation: In both cases, jump ball violation by A2. Team B awarded throw-in close to centre line: from (a) frontcourt with 14 seconds on shot clock, or (b) backcourt with 24 seconds on shot clock. Team A gets first alternating possession.

examples.text: The crew chief tosses the ball for the opening jump ball. Immediately after the ball is legally tapped by jumper A1: (a) a held ball between A2 and B2 occurs; (b) a double foul between A2 and B2 occurs.
examples.interpretation: As live-ball control was not yet established, alternating possession cannot be used. The crew chief administers another jump ball in the centre circle between A2 and B2; consumed game clock remains valid.

examples.text: After the opening jump ball is legally tapped by A1, the ball (a) goes directly out-of-bounds or (b) is caught by A1 before touching another player or the court.
examples.interpretation: Violation by A1. Team B gets throw-in (24s if backcourt, 14s if frontcourt). Once at disposal, team A gets first alternating possession arrow.

examples.text: Immediately after the opening jump ball is legally tapped by A1, B1 is charged with a category 1 technical foul.
examples.interpretation: Any team A player attempts 1 FT (no line-up), placing the alternating possession arrow in favour of team B. Game resumes with team B alternating possession throw-in nearest to where the ball was located (24s backcourt / 14s frontcourt).

examples.text: Immediately after the opening jump ball is legally tapped by A1, A2 is charged with a flagrant foul committed against B2.
examples.interpretation: B2 attempts 2 FTs (no line-up), placing the alternating possession arrow in favour of team A. Game resumes with team B frontcourt throw-in opposite scorer’s table (14s).

examples.text: Team B is entitled to a throw-in under alternating possession, but an error awards it to team A.
examples.interpretation: After the ball touches or is legally touched on court, the error cannot be corrected. Team B does NOT lose its right to the next alternating possession throw-in.

examples.text: Simultaneously with Q1 end signal (referees decide signal sounded first), B1 commits (a) a disruptive foul or (b) a flagrant foul against A1. Team A has AP arrow to start Q2.
examples.interpretation: (a) A disruptive foul cannot occur during an interval of play and is disregarded; Q2 starts with team A AP throw-in from centre line extended (24s). (b) Flagrant foul is NOT disregarded: A1 attempts 2 FTs before Q2, resumed with team A frontcourt throw-in opposite table (14s); Team A keeps its AP arrow.

examples.text: Shortly after Q3 ends, B1 is charged with a category 1 technical foul. Team A has the AP arrow to start Q4.
examples.interpretation: Any team A player attempts 1 FT (no line-up) before Q4; Q4 starts with team A AP throw-in from centre line extended (24s).

examples.text: A1 jumps with ball and is legally blocked by B1; both return to floor with 1 or 2 hands firmly on ball.
examples.interpretation: This is a jump ball situation.

examples.text: A1 jumps with ball and is legally blocked by B1; A1 returns to floor still holding ball while B1 is no longer touching it.
examples.interpretation: This is a travelling violation by A1.

examples.text: A1 and B1 in the air hold ball firmly together; A1 lands with 1 foot on boundary line.
examples.interpretation: This is a jump ball situation.

examples.text: A1 jumps in frontcourt and is blocked by B1; both land holding ball firmly, A1 with 1 foot in backcourt.
examples.interpretation: This is a jump ball situation.

examples.text: Live ball lodged between ring and backboard is a jump ball situation (unless between FTs or before possession penalty): under AP, 14s if offensive team gets throw-in, 24s if defensive team gets throw-in.
During A1’s shot, ball lodges between ring and backboard; AP throw-in awarded to (a) team A or (b) team B.
examples.interpretation: After throw-in behind endline in team B’s backcourt: (a) team A gets 14s; (b) team B gets 24s on the shot clock.

examples.text: A1’s shot is in the air when shot clock horn sounds, then ball lodges between ring and backboard; AP favours team A.
examples.interpretation: Jump ball situation; after throw-in from behind endline in its frontcourt, team A has 14s on shot clock.

examples.text: B2 commits a disruptive or flagrant foul against A1; on A1’s last FT (no line-up): (a) ball lodges between ring and backboard, (b) A1 steps on FT line on release, or (c) ball misses ring.
examples.interpretation: In all cases, FT is unsuccessful. Resumed with team A throw-in from frontcourt throw-in line opposite scorer’s table with 14s.

examples.text: After A1’s throw-in from centre line extended to start a quarter, ball lodges between ring and backboard in team A’s frontcourt.
examples.interpretation: Jump ball situation. AP arrow reverses immediately to team B. Team B gets throw-in from behind its endline (not directly behind backboard) with 24s.

examples.text: AP arrow favours team A. In interval after Q1, B1 commits flagrant foul against A1 (2 FTs + throw-in at frontcourt line). After that throw-in, ball lodges in team A frontcourt.
examples.interpretation: Team A kept its AP arrow through the flagrant throw-in, so now gets AP throw-in behind frontcourt endline with 14s, and arrow reverses to B once throw-in ends.

examples.text: A held ball occurs when one or more players from opposing teams have one or both hands firmly on the ball so that neither player can gain control without undue roughness.
A1 on a drive in act of shooting has B1 place hands firmly on ball and A1 now takes more steps than allowed.
examples.interpretation: This is a jump ball situation.

examples.text: A violation by a team during its alternating possession throw-in causes that team to lose the alternating possession throw-in.
During an AP throw-in at 4:17: (a) A1 steps onto court holding ball, (b) A2 reaches over boundary line, or (c) A1 takes > 5 seconds.
examples.interpretation: Throw-in violation. Team B awarded throw-in from same spot, and AP arrow immediately reverses in favour of team B.

examples.text: Whenever a jump ball situation occurs with no time remaining on the shot clock and the AP arrow favours team A, AP is NOT applied — this is a shot clock violation awarding the ball to team B.
A1’s shot is in the air when shot clock sounds, then (a) enters basket, (b) rebounds off ring -> held ball, or (c) misses ring -> held ball.
examples.interpretation: (a) Goal counts. (b) AP arrow applies (14s if A, 24s if B). (c) Shot clock violation: ignore arrow, team B throw-in with 24s.

examples.text: A1’s shot is in air when shot clock sounds: (a) enters, (b) hits ring and rebounds, or (c) misses ring; immediately after, A2 or B2 commits a technical foul of any category.
examples.interpretation: 1 FT for technical foul first. Then (a) goal counts, B endline; (b) AP throw-in where ball located (14s if A, 24s if B); (c) shot clock violation, team B throw-in (24s).

subPoints.heading: Hands only; deliberate kick / fist strike
subPoints.body: Ball is played with hand(s) only. Deliberately touching, kicking or blocking with any part of leg, or striking with fist is a violation (accidental leg contact is legal). Penalty: opponents’ throw-in nearest to infraction.

examples.text: During the game, ball is played with hands only. It is a violation if a player places the ball between the legs to fake a pass or shot, or deliberately uses head, fist, legs or feet to play the ball.
A1 ends a dribble, places the ball between the legs and fakes a pass or shot.
examples.interpretation: This is a violation by A1 for illegally touching the ball with the leg.

examples.text: A1 passes to A2 on a fast break; before catching, A2 deliberately heads the ball.
examples.interpretation: This is a violation by A2 for illegally using the head to play the ball.

examples.text: It is not permitted to increase a player’s height or reach. It is a violation to lift a team-mate to play the ball.
A1 lifts team-mate A2 under opponents’ basket; A3 passes to A2 who dunks.
examples.interpretation: Violation by team A. Goal does not count; team B throw-in from free-throw line extended in backcourt.

subPoints.heading: Start, continuation, and end of team control
subPoints.body: Starts when a player holds, dribbles, or has a live ball at disposal; continues during passes between team-mates; ends when opponent gains control, ball becomes dead, or ball leaves hands on a shot or free throw.

examples.text: Team control starts when a player of that team is in control of a live ball by holding or dribbling it or has a live ball at the disposal for a throw-in or a free throw.
A player deliberately delays taking the ball for a throw-in or free throw.
examples.interpretation: The ball becomes live and team control starts when the referee places the ball on the floor nearest the throw-in spot or at the free-throw line.

examples.text: Team A has 15s of ball control. A1 passes over sideline; airborne B1 jumps from inbounds over boundary line and (a) taps the ball back or (b) catches with two hands/rests in one hand and throws it back, where A2 catches it.
examples.interpretation: (a) Team A stayed in control -> remaining shot clock time. (b) B1 gained control for team B, then A2 regained new team A control -> new 24 seconds.

articles.title: Player in the act of shooting

subPoints.heading: Shot, tap and dunk
subPoints.body: Shot throws ball into air from hand(s); tap directs ball with hand(s); dunk forces ball downwards with one or both hands.

subPoints.heading: Jump shots vs. continuous movement drives
subPoints.body: On jump shots: starts when shoulders and ball move upwards toward basket. On drives (frontcourt, gathering dribble/air catch): starts when ball is gathered and comes to rest in hand(s) and shooting motion continues. Ends when ball leaves hand(s), new act begins, or airborne shooter’s both feet return to floor.

subPoints.heading: Frontcourt requirement, clock exception & pass-off rule
subPoints.body: Must be in frontcourt (except last action anywhere on court before game/shot clock expiration). No link between legal steps and act of shooting (15.1.5). Passing off after being fouled (or moving ball away/not facing basket on jump shots) cancels act-of-shooting status (15.1.7–15.1.8).

examples.text: The act of shooting on jump shots or other moving shots starts when the player begins to move the shoulders and the ball upwards towards the opponents’ basket.
A1 dribbles between 3-point line and restricted area, stops legally with both feet down without moving ball upwards, and B1 fouls A1.
examples.interpretation: B1’s foul is NOT in the act of shooting.

examples.text: A1 catches near FT line, faces basket, starts moving shoulders and ball upwards for jump shot, and is fouled by B1 before release.
examples.interpretation: Act of shooting: goal counts + 1 FT if made; 2 FTs if missed.

examples.text: A1 catches while moving laterally outside 3-point line, begins turning toward basket while moving shoulders and ball upwards, and is fouled before release.
examples.interpretation: Act of shooting applies because upward movement of shoulders and ball towards the basket had begun before the foul.

examples.text: With 6:25 in Q2 (20s shot clock) on fast break, A1 completes dribble and gathers ball between centre line and 3-point line in frontcourt; fouled by B1 before upward motion.
examples.interpretation: NOT in act of shooting: due to court location (outside 3PT area, not a continuous drive from inside 3PT line), drive-to-basket continuous movement does not apply.

examples.text: A1 jumps and releases 3-point shot; B1 fouls A1 before both feet return to floor; shot misses.
examples.interpretation: Shooter remains in act of shooting until both feet return to floor -> 3 free throws.

examples.text: The act of shooting in a continuous movement on drives to the basket starts when the player has gathered the ball and it comes to rest in the player’s hands upon completion of a dribble or air catch and continues the shooting motion.
A1 drives between 3-point line and basket, gathers ball and starts shooting motion; B1 fouls A1; shot misses.
examples.interpretation: Foul in act of shooting -> 2 free throws.

examples.text: A1 on a drive pushes off B1 with one hand while holding ball in the other, then throws ball into basket.
examples.interpretation: Team control foul by A1; goal disallowed; team B throw-in from FT line extended in backcourt.

examples.text: B1 fouls driving A1 with front foot on floor; contact briefly dislodges ball from A1’s hands, A1 re-gathers with both hands and scores.
examples.interpretation: A1 remained in control during continuous act of shooting -> goal counts + 1 FT.

examples.text: Continuous movement on drives to basket typically starts in frontcourt between offensive 3-point line and basket.
A1 drives from outside 3-point line, gathers ball with one foot on court, fouled before release.
examples.interpretation: Act of shooting on a drive; number of legal steps taken after gather is irrelevant.

examples.text: A1 starts drive 1 m behind 3-point line, gathers with left foot on 3-point line, takes two steps along restricted area, fouled by B1 right at the gather.
examples.interpretation: Act of shooting on drives begins at the gather when ball comes to rest in hands.

examples.text: For a player to be in the act of shooting, the player must be in the frontcourt (except clock-expiration last action).
With 18s on shot clock, A1 gathers ball in backcourt and throws toward basket; B1 fouls A1 on gather.
examples.interpretation: NOT in act of shooting because player is in backcourt and clock is not expiring.

examples.text: With 2 seconds left in Q2, A1 catches in backcourt, starts shooting motion toward opponents’ basket, fouled by B1.
examples.interpretation: Act of shooting applies anywhere on court for last action before quarter/overtime clock expires (starts on gather).

examples.text: With 2:33 game clock / 0.9s shot clock in Q3, A1 catches in backcourt, starts shooting motion, fouled by B1 on gather or upward motion.
examples.interpretation: Act of shooting applies anywhere on court immediately before shot clock expiration.

examples.text: When a player in act of shooting on jump/moving shots passes the ball off after being fouled, the player is no longer in act of shooting.
B1 (3rd team foul) fouls shooter A1, after which A1 passes to A2.
examples.interpretation: Act of shooting ended upon pass-off -> team A throw-in nearest foul.

examples.text: If fouled in act of shooting and shooter scores while committing a travelling violation, goal does not count and 2 or 3 FTs are awarded.
Driving A1 is fouled by B1, then travels and scores 2-point basket.
examples.interpretation: Goal disallowed; A1 attempts 2 free throws.

examples.text: On jump shots or other moving shots, if after being fouled the player is NOT facing the basket when moving the ball upwards, that player is no longer considered in act of shooting.
A1 faces away from basket when shoulders and ball move upward; B1 (3rd team foul) fouls A1; A1 scores.
examples.interpretation: Not in act of shooting -> goal cancelled; team A throw-in nearest foul.

examples.text: Low-post A1 with back to basket moves ball upward before turning to face basket and is fouled by B1.
examples.interpretation: Not in act of shooting because A1 was not facing basket during upward motion.

examples.text: A1 rebounds under basket, back to basket while looking up at basket, makes reverse shot; fouled by B1 in upward motion.
examples.interpretation: Act of shooting: by looking up at basket, A1 is considered facing the basket.

examples.text: A1 runs along endline, catches, jumps looking up at basket for reverse shot; pushed by B1 during upward motion.
examples.interpretation: Act of shooting: looking up at basket constitutes facing the basket.

articles.title: Goal: When made and its value

subPoints.heading: Definition of made goal
subPoints.body: Live ball enters basket from above and remains within or passes through completely. Ball is within basket when slightest part is inside and below ring level.

subPoints.heading: Point values & own-basket rules
subPoints.body: FT = 1 pt, 2PT area = 2 pts, 3PT area = 3 pts, tip-in after ring on last FT = 2 pts. Accidental own basket = 2 pts for opposing captain on court; deliberate own basket or ball passing from below = violation.

subPoints.heading: 0.3 s / 0.2 s / 0.1 s rule
subPoints.body: Minimum 0.3 s required to catch-and-shoot on throw-in or last-FT rebound. With 0.2 s or 0.1 s showing, only a tap or direct dunk (released before 0.0) can count.

examples.text: Goal value is defined by where shot was released: 2-point area = 2 pts, 3-point area = 3 pts.
A1 shoots from 3-point area; ball on upward flight is legally touched by a player in 2-point area and enters basket.
examples.interpretation: 3 points awarded (shot was released from 3-point area).

examples.text: A1 shoots from 2-point area; ball on upward flight is legally touched by B1 who jumped from 3-point area and enters basket.
examples.interpretation: 2 points awarded (shot was released from 2-point area).

examples.text: At start of quarter, B1 erroneously dribbles into own basket and scores.
examples.interpretation: 2 points awarded to opposing team A captain on court.

examples.text: If a pass enters opponents’ basket directly or after touching a player/court, point value depends on where the pass was released.
A1 passes from 3-point area; ball enters basket (a) directly or (b) after touching player or court.
examples.interpretation: 3 points awarded in both cases (released from 3-point area).

examples.text: A1 shoots from 3-point area; ball bounces on floor inside 2-point area then enters basket.
examples.interpretation: 3 points awarded.

examples.text: B1 fouls A1 shooting 3-pointer; ball touches court then enters basket.
examples.interpretation: Goal disallowed (shot ended when touching floor, so ball became dead on whistle) -> A1 shoots 3 FTs.

examples.text: A1 shoots 3-pointer; quarter horn sounds in flight; ball hits floor then bounces in.
examples.interpretation: Goal disallowed (shot ended on floor touch and became dead on horn).

examples.text: Thrower-in A1 passes from out-of-bounds in frontcourt; ball is legally touched inside 3-point area and enters basket.
examples.interpretation: Counts 2 points (3 points only from on-court shot/pass behind 3-point line).

examples.text: Minimum 0.3s needed to catch-and-shoot on throw-in/rebound; with 0.2s or 0.1s only a tap or direct dunk (released before 0.0) can count.
Team A throw-in with (a) 0.3s or (b) 0.2/0.1s remaining.
examples.interpretation: (a) Referees determine if shot left hands before horn. (b) Only tap or direct dunk counts.

examples.text: At quarter end A1 dunks directly; ball still touches A1’s hands at 0.0.
examples.interpretation: Goal does not count.

examples.text: Game clock stops immediately upon made basket when (a) defensive team requested a time-out or (b) game clock shows <= 2:00 in Q4 or OT.
A1 scores at 2:02 in Q4; B1 is ready for endline throw-in at 2:00.
examples.interpretation: Goal was scored with > 2:00 left -> game clock is NOT stopped.

subPoints.heading: Definition (17.1.1 – 17.1.2)
subPoints.body: Starts at thrower-in’s disposal; ends when ball touches/is touched by player on court, team commits violation, or live ball lodges between ring and backboard.

subPoints.heading: Procedure & throw-in spots (17.2.1 – 17.2.10)
subPoints.body: Referee passes <= 4 m away or hands ball. Specific restart rules apply:
bullets: 17.2.3 Q2/Q3/Q4/OT start: centre line extended opposite table.
17.2.4 Last 2:00 Q4/OT timeout from backcourt: head coach chooses frontcourt throw-in line (choice of side after made basket; same side after foul/violation/JB) or backcourt.
17.2.7 Disruptive, flagrant, or disqualifying foul: frontcourt throw-in line opposite scorer’s table.
17.2.10 After made goal/last FT: anywhere behind endline; lateral movement & out-of-bounds passes permitted (5s starts at first disposal).

subPoints.heading: Restrictions, 2:00 warning & penalty (17.3.1 – 17.4)
subPoints.body: 5s limit; cannot step onto court, enter basket directly, or move > 1 m laterally from fixed spot (may move straight back). Other players may not reach over boundary line or stand < 1 m away if OOB space < 2 m. Under 2:00 Q4/OT, referee gives illegal-crossing warning signal — crossing/intruding then causes a violation leading to a technical foul (17.3.3).

examples.text: Players other than thrower-in shall not have any body part over boundary line; defender must avoid contacting ball even if thrower-in’s hands cross line during motion.
Backcourt throw-in in Q3: (a) A1 moves hands over line and B1 grabs/taps ball without contact; (b) B1 reaches hands over line toward A1.
examples.interpretation: Delay-of-game throw-in violation by B1 + verbal/signal warning to B1 & head coach for whole team B (repetition = Cat 2 Technical Foul). Repeat throw-in (24s).

examples.text: Frontcourt throw-in in Q3 with (a) 7s or (b) 17s on shot clock; B1 reaches hands over boundary line.
examples.interpretation: Violation + delay-of-game warning for whole team B (repetition = Cat 2 Tech). Repeat throw-in with (a) 14s or (b) 17s on shot clock.

examples.text: Under <= 2:00 in Q4/OT, defensive player shall not move any body part over boundary line to interfere with throw-in.
At 0:54 Q4, referee shows illegal boundary line crossing warning signal; B1 then reaches over line before throw-in.
examples.interpretation: B1 charged immediately with a Category 2 Technical Foul.

examples.text: At 0:51 Q4, referee did NOT show warning signal first; B1 reaches over boundary line.
examples.interpretation: Stop play, give B1/coach team-wide warning (repetition = Cat 2 Tech), repeat throw-in and show warning signal.

examples.text: Thrower-in must pass (never hand) ball to a team-mate on the court.
Thrower-in A1 hands ball directly to A2 on the court.
examples.interpretation: Throw-in violation by A1 -> team B throw-in from same spot.

examples.text: After infraction vs. after made basket/timeout: thrower-in hands ball to team-mate (17-10) vs. passes along endline behind endline (17-11).
examples.interpretation: After infraction (17-10), receiver stepping OOB violates Art. 17.3. After made basket/FT (even after timeout, 17-11), teammates may pass/hand/move behind endline within the 5-second count.

examples.text: Last 2:00 Q4/OT backcourt timeout advancement (17-12 statement & scenarios 17-13 to 17-21).
examples.interpretation: Coach states loudly "frontcourt" or "backcourt" and points (final & irreversible even after extra timeouts, 17-21). Made basket -> coach picks either side; foul/violation/JB -> same side. Frontcourt throw-in line gets 14s (or remaining <= 13s if OOB/Tech); backcourt keeps 17-19s on OOB/double-foul or gets 24s on foul/kick.

examples.text: Centre line extended starts vs. infractions on centre line vs. disruptive/flagrant/DQ frontcourt throw-in line.
examples.interpretation: Quarter/OT throw-in violation repeats from centre line extended with AP reversed (17-23); infraction on court centre line uses frontcourt side 14s (17-25); DI/FL/DQ throw-in always opposite scorer’s table in frontcourt with 14s (17-26, 17-27).

examples.text: Reaching through basket on throw-in (17-29), ball wedged on throw-in (17-30), bouncing ball inbounds (17-32), throwing OOB (17-34), catching on line (17-35), lateral 1m step crossing centre line (17-36).
examples.interpretation: Reaching through hoop = basket interference (no pts from OOB, FT line ext); bouncing on inbounds then catching = violation (17-32a), bouncing OOB <= 1m lateral = legal (17-32b); thrower taking 1m lateral step across centre extension keeps original pass rights (17-36).

examples.text: Endline mobility after made goal (17-37, 17-38 defender delay), kick ball after endline pass cancels run-endline right (17-39), airborne teammate jump from behind endline (17-40).
examples.interpretation: Teammates behind endline retain endline movement even after defensive throw-in interference warning (17-38), but lose it once ball touches court before kick violation (17-39). Jumping from OOB and landing inbounds before releasing is a violation (17-40d/e).

examples.text: Resumption after technical fouls (17-41–17-49) and invalid goal/last FT free-throw line extended spots (17-50–17-52).
examples.interpretation: Tech by team in control keeps same shot clock (unless <= 2:00 TO moved to frontcourt -> cap 14s, 17-45); tech by defense resets 24s backcourt or max(remaining,14s) frontcourt. Invalid FT by shooter -> FT line extended opposite table; invalid goal -> same side where cancelled (17-50).

subPoints.heading: Allowance & last 2:00 cap (18.2.1 – 18.2.8)
subPoints.body: 1 minute duration. Each team gets 2 in first half, 3 in second half (max 2 when clock <= 2:00 in Q4), and 1 per OT (no carry-over). Not granted to scoring team after a goal in <= 2:00 Q4/OT unless referee stops play.

subPoints.heading: Procedure & during free throws (18.3.1 – 18.3.6)
subPoints.body: Requested only by head coach or first assistant coach; cancellable only before timer’s signal. Requested during FTs is granted after successful last FT or throw-in follow-up.

examples.text: No timeout before clock starts on opening jump/violation (18/19-2); shot-clock horn while ball in air on made shot (18/19-4).
examples.interpretation: Cannot grant TO/sub before game clock starts (18/19-2). Made shot with simultaneous shot-clock horn is a timeout opportunity ONLY for non-scoring team (18/19-4a).

examples.text: Timeout/substitution requests during free throws (18/19-6, 18/19-7) and after goaltending/interference (18/19-9).
examples.interpretation: Once ball is at FT shooter’s disposal for 1st FT, requests are only granted if last FT is made, followed by throw-in, or dead after violation; NOT granted between FTs or on live rebound (18/19-7a).

examples.text: Foul communication before timeout clock starts (18/19-16, 18/19-17) and extending 1-minute timeout / late return from half-time (18/19-18–18/19-20).
examples.interpretation: Timeout starts only after foul/5th-foul sub reporting completes. Delay returning after re-beckon incurs extra charged TO (or B1 Cat 1 Tech if none left); late after half-time incurs immediate un-timed charged TO without warning (18/19-20).

examples.text: 2:00 fourth quarter first half-2 TO forfeiture (18/19-21–18/19-23) and timeout priority before DI/FL/DQ/T free throws (18/19-24–18/19-26).
examples.interpretation: At 2:00 Q4, first unused 2nd-half timeout box is crossed (even if coach requested at 2:09 while clock ran, 18/19-23). Any requested timeout is ALWAYS granted BEFORE administering technical/disruptive/flagrant/DQ free throws (18/19-24).

subPoints.heading: Opportunities & re-entry lock (19.2.1 – 19.2.6)
subPoints.body: Opportunity starts on dead ball/clock stopped (or after made goal <= 2:00 Q4/OT for non-scoring team only). Incoming/outgoing players cannot swap again until ball becomes dead after a clock-running period.

subPoints.heading: Procedure & 30 s limit (19.3.1 – 19.3.9)
subPoints.body: Only the substitute requests at table/chair. 5-foul or disqualified players must be substituted within 30 s or face delay timeout / coach technical foul (B). Substitute must shoot injury/5-foul/DQ FTs before being eligible to sub out next clock-running stoppage (19.3.8).

examples.text: Technical foul between free throws & sub becoming FT shooter (18/19-10–18/19-13); sub foul before clock restarts (18/19-14–18/19-15).
examples.interpretation: Substitute may become player only if attempting the tech FT (opponent then gets 1 sub, 18/19-10). Incoming player who commits 3rd foul before clock starts cannot sub out; 5th foul MUST sub out (18/19-15).

subPoints.heading: Conditions & 20–0 penalty
subPoints.body: Forfeit if a team is absent/unable to field 5 ready players 15 min after scheduled start, prevents play, or refuses to play after crew chief instruction. Score recorded 20–0 (0 classification points); 2nd forfeit in a tournament disqualifies team and nullifies all its games.

examples.text: Team 4A in group A is not present with 5 players 15 minutes after scheduled start (first forfeit), and forfeits a second game in the tournament (Appendix D.3.3).
examples.interpretation: First forfeit = 20–0 loss and 0 classification points. Second forfeit in a tournament = team 4A is disqualified and all results of games played by 4A are nullified.

subPoints.heading: Fewer than 2 players on court
subPoints.body: Occurs during the game when a team has fewer than 2 players on court ready to play. Score stands if non-defaulting team leads, otherwise 2–0; defaulting team receives 1 classification point.

examples.text: Late in Q4, due to 5th fouls and injuries, Team A is reduced to only 1 eligible player remaining on the court while leading 68–62 (or trailing 55–62).
examples.interpretation: Game ends by default (< 2 players). Since Team B wins by default: if Team B was ahead (62–55) the score stands; if Team B was behind (62–68) the official score becomes 2–0 for Team B. Team A receives 1 classification point.

subPoints.heading: Definition and general penalty
subPoints.body: A violation is an infraction of the rules. Penalty: opponents’ throw-in from nearest place (except directly behind backboard), unless stated otherwise.

examples.text: A1 steps on the baseline behind the opponent’s backboard while holding a live ball.
examples.interpretation: Out-of-bounds violation: ball is awarded to Team B for a throw-in from the place nearest the infraction, EXCEPT never from directly behind the backboard (shift laterally to the nearest spot along the endline).

subPoints.heading: Definitions (23.1.1 – 23.1.2)
subPoints.body: Player is OOB when any body part touches floor/object above, on or outside boundary line. Ball is OOB when touching OOB player/person, floor/object OOB, or backboard supports/back of backboard.

subPoints.heading: Rule & held ball exception (23.2.1 – 23.2.3)
subPoints.body: Last player to touch/be touched causes OOB. If a player moves OOB or to backcourt during a held ball, a jump ball situation occurs (23.2.3).

examples.text: If the ball is out-of-bounds because of touching or being touched by a player who is on or outside the boundary line, this player causes the ball to go out-of-bounds.
Close to sideline, A1 holding ball contacts B1’s body while B1 has 1 foot out-of-bounds.
examples.interpretation: Legal play by A1; game continues (player OOB, not ball).

examples.text: A1 holding ball touches B1 WITH THE BALL while B1 has 1 foot out-of-bounds.
examples.interpretation: Out-of-bounds violation by B1 -> team A throw-in nearest spot with remaining shot clock time.

examples.text: A1 dribbles near sideline; ball bounces high and touches substitute B6’s knee on substitution chair, then returns to court to A1.
examples.interpretation: Ball went out-of-bounds when touching B6; caused OOB by A1 (last inbounds player to touch ball) -> team B throw-in.

subPoints.heading: Start, carrying & fumbles (24.1.1 – 24.1.4)
subPoints.body: Dribble starts when player throws, taps, rolls or bounces live ball on court and touches it again before another player. Placing hand under ball (carrying/palming) or pausing and continuing is illegal. Unlimited steps while ball is out of hand. Fumbles, taps to gain control, deflections, throwing against backboard and regaining are not dribbles.

subPoints.heading: Second dribble prohibition
subPoints.body: No second dribble after first dribble ends unless control was lost via a shot, opponent touch, or pass/fumble touched by another player.

examples.text: It is not a dribble if a player deliberately throws the ball against either the opponents’ or the team’s own backboard.
A1 has not yet dribbled, throws ball deliberately against backboard and catches/touches it before another player.
examples.interpretation: Legal play; after catching, A1 may shoot, pass, or start a dribble.

examples.text: After ending a dribble, A1 deliberately throws ball against backboard and catches/touches it again (a) after it bounced on court and starts a dribble, or (b) before it touches any other player.
examples.interpretation: (a) Double dribble violation. (b) Legal play — may shoot or pass, NOT start a new dribble.

examples.text: A1’s shot misses ring; A1 catches rebound, throws deliberately off backboard and catches again.
examples.interpretation: Legal play; A1 may shoot, pass, or start a dribble.

examples.text: Loss of control exceptions (24-5), touching floor while holding ball / tossing hand-to-hand without moving pivot (24-6), throwing ball over/past opponent onto floor to start dribble (24-7).
examples.interpretation: Touching floor while holding ball or tossing hand-to-hand without moving pivot foot is legal (24-6). Throwing ball over opponent to bounce on floor starts a legal dribble (24-7).

examples.text: Ending dribble and (24-8) throwing against B1’s leg; (24-9) fumbling onto B2/A2’s leg; (24-10) pass accidentally hitting B2’s body; (24-11) B1 touching ball while still in A1’s hands.
examples.interpretation: 24-8: Double dribble (ball touched B1, not B1 touching ball). 24-9 & 24-10: Legal new dribble after fumble/pass touched another player. 24-11: A1 kept control -> cannot dribble again.

subPoints.heading: Definitions (25.1.1 – 25.1.2)
subPoints.body: Illegal movement of one or both feet while holding a live ball. A pivot steps once or more with one foot while keeping the pivot foot at its contact point.

subPoints.heading: Establishing pivot foot & 2-step gather rule
subPoints.body: Standing catch: lifting one foot makes the other pivot; pivot foot cannot be lifted before ball release to start a dribble, but may jump off pivot to pass/shoot (no foot may return before release). Catch while progressing / after dribble: 2 steps permitted; dribble must start before step 2; step 1 = first foot/feet touching after control.

subPoints.heading: Falling, lying or sitting on court
subPoints.body: Falling and sliding while holding the ball (or gaining control while lying/sitting) is legal; rolling or attempting to stand up while holding the ball is a travelling violation.

examples.text: A1 holds ball, loses balance, falls and slides due to momentum (25-2).
examples.interpretation: Falling and sliding from momentum is legal; rolling to evade defense or attempting to stand while holding ball is a travelling violation.

examples.text: While lying on court, A1 gains control and (a) passes, (b) starts dribble while lying, (c) stands up while dribbling, or (d) attempts to stand up holding ball.
examples.interpretation: (a), (b) and (c) are legal; (d) is a travelling violation.

examples.text: After ending a dribble, A1 jumps off left foot, lands on LEFT foot, then right foot, and shoots (25-5).
examples.interpretation: Travelling violation: may not touch court consecutively with the same foot after ending dribble.

subPoints.heading: Restricted area limit & allowances
subPoints.body: Maximum 3 consecutive seconds in opponents’ restricted area during frontcourt team control with clock running. Allowances: attempting to leave, teammate/self in act of shooting as ball leaves hands, or dribbling in to shoot after < 3s. Both feet must be placed outside to clear the count.

examples.text: A1 in restricted area < 3s steps OOB at endline to reset count, then re-enters paint (26-2).
examples.interpretation: 3-second violation by A1.

examples.text: A1 in paint 2.5s shoots airball and rebounds it (26-4); A2 stands in paint > 3s while thrower-in A1 holds ball OOB (26-5).
examples.interpretation: Both legal: shot ends team control releasing 3s count (26-4); during throw-in, game clock is stopped so 3s does not apply (26-5).

subPoints.heading: 1 metre / 5 seconds rule
subPoints.body: Holding (not dribbling) a live ball within 1 m of an active legal defender requires passing, shooting, or dribbling within 5 seconds.

examples.text: Closely guarded for 4s by B1, A1 fumbles ball and catches it again, reaching 5s total.
examples.interpretation: 5-second violation (fumbling is not a dribble).

subPoints.heading: Backcourt advancement & continuations
subPoints.body: Team must advance live ball into frontcourt within 8 seconds (ball touches frontcourt, offensive player has both feet in frontcourt, or defender/referee with body in backcourt/frontcourt respectively). Count continues with remaining time after same-team OOB, injury, team technical foul, jump ball, double foul, or equal cancellations (28.1.3).

examples.text: A1 dribbles in backcourt for 5s -> held ball -> AP throw-in awarded to team A.
examples.interpretation: Team A has only 3 seconds remaining to enter frontcourt.

examples.text: A1 straddling centre line passes back to A2 (28-4); dribbler stops while straddling or with both feet in frontcourt while ball bounces in backcourt (28-5).
examples.interpretation: Legal: both feet of dribbler AND ball must be completely in frontcourt before frontcourt status is reached; 8s continues.

examples.text: Referee must inform thrower-in of remaining 8s time after backcourt double foul (28-7a), defender OOB tap (28-8), or unrelated stoppage like bottle thrown / clock error with 3s left (28-10).
examples.interpretation: 8s count continues with remaining time in all same-team backcourt continuations and when defense would be disadvantaged by an unrelated stoppage (28-10).

examples.text: 8-second violation when (a) A1 holds ball in backcourt vs. (b) ball is in air on pass from backcourt to frontcourt.
examples.interpretation: Team B frontcourt throw-in (14s) nearest (a) ball’s location when 8s expired or (b) centre line.

subPoints.heading: 24-second shot requirement
subPoints.body: Ball must leave shooter’s hands before signal AND subsequently touch ring or enter basket. If shot in flight misses ring after horn, it is a violation UNLESS opponents gain immediate clear control (29.1.2). Top yellow backboard LED takes precedence over horn.

subPoints.heading: 24 s / 14 s resets on stoppages
subPoints.body: Same-team retention in backcourt resets to 24 s; in frontcourt keeps time if >= 14 s, or resets to 14 s if <= 13 s (29.2.2). New team control after foul/violation or AP resets to 24 s in backcourt or 14 s in frontcourt (29.2.3).

subPoints.heading: Technical foul, <= 2:00 advancement, ring reset & error signal
subPoints.body: Tech by team in control keeps clock unchanged (29.2.4). After <= 2:00 timeout advancing ball to frontcourt throw-in line: OOB with <= 13 s stays as-is, >= 14 s resets to 14 s; new control or foul/violation resets to 14 s (29.2.5). Disruptive/flagrant/DQ frontcourt throw-in resets to 14 s (29.2.6). After touching ring: 24 s for defense, 14 s for offensive rebound (29.2.7).

examples.text: Shot clock horn while shot is in air: hits backboard then touches B1 then A2 then B2 (29/51-2); legal block by B1 then foul after horn (29/51-4); misses ring -> held ball or OOB tap (29/51-5).
examples.interpretation: Shot clock violation unless shot hits ring OR opponents gain IMMEDIATE and clear control. Foul after shot-clock violation is disregarded unless flagrant or disqualifying (29/51-4).

examples.text: Shooting foul near shot-clock expiration (29/51-6 a–d); shot-clock violation timing vs game clock adjustment (29/51-7, 29/51-8).
examples.interpretation: If ball already left hands OR foul occurred before shot clock expired -> goal counts + 1 FT (missed = 2/3 FTs). If shot still in hands & foul after horn -> shot clock violation, reset game clock to exact time of violation (e.g., 1.2s in 29/51-8).

examples.text: Loose pass rolls into backcourt, shot clock sounds right as B1 has clear fast-break pickup (29/51-10) vs. deflected endline pass before horn (29/51-11).
examples.interpretation: Immediate clear opponent control disregards horn (29/51-10); mere deflection while team A remains in control still triggers violation (29/51-11).

examples.text: Same-team AP throws keep 10s (29/51-13); frontcourt OOB keeps 8s vs foul gives 14s (29/51-15); B1 injury gives 14s vs A1 injury keeps 4s (29/51-16); kick ball reset check 16s vs 12s (29/51-19); DI/FL/DQ reset 14s (29/51-20).
examples.interpretation: Out-of-bounds, own injury, own technical, AP/double/cancelled fouls keep time if <= 13s; opponent foul/violation/injury raises <= 13s up to 14s (stays 16s if >= 14s). DI/FL/DQ throw-in line always sets 14s.

examples.text: Unrelated stoppage with 4s left (29/51-22); shot clock failed to reset after hitting ring, error spotted 9s later -> 5s left (29/51-23); erroneous 14s reset on airball followed by made basket (29/51-24).
examples.interpretation: Reset clock to exact remaining time (4s in 29/51-22; 5s in 29/51-23). If airball reset wrongly caused score after true 24s would have expired -> shot clock violation, cancel goal (29/51-24).

examples.text: Shot in air + foul against defender in backcourt away from play (29/51-26–29/51-31: with 17s, with 10s, or after shot-clock horn).
examples.interpretation: Shot counts if made; non-penalty throw-in keeps >= 14s (17s) or resets <= 13s to 14s (even after horn on airborne shot, 29/51-29). In 5th team foul, 2 FTs replace throw-in.

examples.text: Offensive rebound off ring / pass hitting ring / tap after ring / OOB off ring / wedged off ring -> 14s (29/51-35–29/51-44) vs. defender gained clear control before losing ball -> 24s (29/51-45).
examples.interpretation: Whenever ball touches opponents’ ring and same team regains control (or gets OOB/AP/rebound foul), shot clock resets to 14s (even on backcourt rebound OOB, 29/51-40). Only clear opponent control grants a fresh 24s (29/51-45).

examples.text: New control anywhere on court = 24s (29/51-48); backcourt OOB turnover -> opponent frontcourt = 14s (29/51-51); < 24s on game clock -> shot clock off, EXCEPT > 14s remaining on game clock after offensive rebound off ring turns 14s ON (29/51-55 vs 29/51-56, 29/51-57).
examples.interpretation: Under 24s game clock, shot clock stays off unless offensive team gets rebound off ring with > 14.0s remaining on game clock, in which case shot clock displays 14s (29/51-55). Missing ring keeps it off (29/51-57).

subPoints.heading: Frontcourt control & airborne exception
subPoints.body: Frontcourt control exists when player touches frontcourt with both feet while holding/catching/dribbling, or during frontcourt passes. Last touched in frontcourt then first touched in backcourt (or by player touching backcourt) is a violation — except a player jumping from frontcourt, gaining NEW team control airborne, and landing in backcourt (30.1.2). Penalty: opponents’ frontcourt throw-in nearest infraction.

examples.text: Airborne intercept exceptions (30-2, 30-3) vs frontcourt throw-in airborne catch (30-4) vs passing to backcourt teammate BEFORE landing (30-5, 30-6).
examples.interpretation: Jumping from frontcourt and establishing NEW team control (or opening jump ball control) while airborne lets the player LAND in backcourt legally, but NOT pass to a teammate in backcourt before landing (30-5, 30-6). On a frontcourt throw-in team control already exists, so landing in backcourt is a violation (30-4).

examples.text: Frontcourt bounce-pass touching backcourt (30-8); backcourt pass hitting frontcourt or referee straddling centre line (30-9, 30-10); simultaneous touch A1/B1 (30-11); dribbling transition & 1-foot catch in frontcourt (30-12–30-17).
examples.interpretation: Simultaneous frontcourt touch by A1 & B1 into backcourt touched by A2 = violation (30-11). Backcourt pass hitting frontcourt/referee resets 8s when A2 catches in backcourt (30-9, 30-10).
