Catching with 1 foot in frontcourt and placing other in backcourt is legal because BOTH feet never touched frontcourt (30-17).

subPoints.heading: Goaltending (shot & free throw)
subPoints.body: Field goal: touching ball completely above ring level while downward to basket or after hitting backboard (until touching ring or losing chance). Free throw: touching ball in flight before touching ring.

subPoints.heading: Basket interference
subPoints.body: Touching basket/backboard while ball is on ring; reaching through basket from below; touching ball/basket while ball is inside basket; vibrating/grasping ring/net unnaturally; touching ball after ring post-whistle/horn while chance remains.

subPoints.heading: Penalties (2026: last FT tech foul)
subPoints.body: Offensive infraction = no score, FT-line extended throw-in. Defensive infraction = 1/2/3 points awarded. Defensive violation during LAST free throw = 1 point awarded + Category 2 Technical Foul against defender (31.3.3).

examples.text: Reaching through basket from below on last FT before ring vs after ring (31-2) and during pass above ring (31-4).
examples.interpretation: During last FT before ring (31-2a): 1 pt + Cat 2 Technical Foul against B1. After touching ring (31-2b): 1 pt, NO technical foul. During pass (31-4): 2 or 3 pts awarded.

examples.text: On last missed FT, ball rebounds off ring and defender B1 tries to tap it out, tapping it into own basket.
examples.interpretation: Legal play (ball already hit ring): opposing captain on court receives 2 points.

examples.text: Post-foul on last FT rebound (31-8–31-11) or post-quarter horn (31-12): A2/B2 touches ball after ring while it still has chance to enter.
examples.interpretation: Basket interference violation by whichever player touches ball (offensive = 0 pts, defensive = 1 or 2/3 pts awarded). Resumption depends on foul/double foul/quarter end.

examples.text: Upward flight / highest point legal touch vs downward flight goaltending (31-14, 31-16); vibrating rim after game-end horn (31-18); touching ring/backboard while ball on ring (31-20); simultaneous touch A2 & B2 on downward flight (31-21).
examples.interpretation: Highest point touch is legal (31-16); downward flight goaltending by both A2 & B2 = 0 pts + AP throw-in (31-21). Vibrating basket after end-of-game horn still penalized (31-18).

examples.text: Grasping ring/net (31-23), ball spinning inside basket with slightest part below rim level (31-25, 31-26, 31-27).
examples.interpretation: Offensive player may legally touch ball spinning inside basket (31-25b, 31-27b) UNLESS clock horn sounded (31-26a). Defensive touch inside basket = 2/3 pts (or 1 pt on FT).

subPoints.heading: Definition & dead-ball disregard
subPoints.body: Illegal personal contact with an opponent and/or unsportsmanlike behaviour. Any number of fouls may be called. Fouls after dead ball (end of quarter/infraction) are disregarded unless technical, flagrant, or disqualifying.

examples.text: Quarter-end horn sounds while A1’s shot is in flight; after the horn, B1 commits normal personal contact against airborne A1.
examples.interpretation: Under Art. 32.1.3, personal contact after a dead-ball quarter-end horn is disregarded — ONLY technical, flagrant, or disqualifying fouls may still be called (when a quarter/OT remains).

subPoints.heading: Cylinder principle
subPoints.body: Imaginary vertical cylinder defined front by palms (or bent knees/arms above hips for ball-handler), rear by buttocks, sides by outer edges of arms/legs. Protects normal basketball play (dribble start, pivot, pass, shoot).

subPoints.heading: Principle of verticality & legal guarding position
subPoints.body: Players may jump vertically within their cylinder; whoever leaves their vertical cylinder causing contact is responsible. Initial legal guarding position: facing opponent + both feet on floor (extends vertically to ceiling).

subPoints.heading: Guarding with vs. without the ball
subPoints.body: With ball (33.4): time and distance do NOT apply; defender may stay stationary, jump vertically, move laterally or backwards (contact must be on torso). Without ball (33.5): time and distance DO apply — never less than 1 normal step.

subPoints.heading: Airborne player, screening, charging & blocking
subPoints.body: Airborne shooter/jumper retains straight landing corridor (undercutting is usually flagrant/disqualifying). Legal screen: stationary in cylinder with both feet down; blind rear screens require 1 normal step; moving targets require 1–2 normal steps.

subPoints.heading: No-charge semi-circle areas (1.30 m)
subPoints.body: Airborne ball-handler driving into no-charge semi-circle who shoots or passes is NOT called for a team control charge against a defender with >= 1 foot touching the semi-circle area (unless illegally using hands/arms/legs/body).

subPoints.heading: Hands, post play, rear guarding, holding, pushing & fake
subPoints.body: Impeding movement with hands/arms, jabbing, offensive hooking/push-off, shoulder/hip displacement in post, rear contact without justification, holding, pushing, and theatrical faking to gain advantage are fouls.

examples.text: Airborne 3-point shooter A1 kicks/extends leg outside cylinder contacting defender B1 (33-2).
examples.interpretation: Foul by A1 (cylinder principle applies equally to offensive & defensive players).

examples.text: No-charge semi-circle cases: normal drive from outside into B1 touching line (33-4); baseline drive behind backboard into semi-circle (33-5); offensive rebound charge (33-6); drop-off pass to trailer vs kickout to corner (33-7 vs 33-8); arm push-off (33-9); defender jumping vertically out of semi-circle (33-10).
examples.interpretation: No-charge rule protects shooter/passer driving from front over arc into grounded defender (33-4, 33-8), EXCEPT: coming from behind backboard (33-5), rebound putback (33-6), clearing path for trailing driver (33-7), illegal arm use (33-9), or when defender jumped legally vertically into the air (33-10).

examples.text: B1 pushes teammate B2 into shooter A1 (33-12) vs B2 pushes A2 into teammate A1 who shoots (33-13).
examples.interpretation: 33-12: B2 caused illegal contact -> A1 shoots + FT on B2 foul. 33-13: A1’s basket counts, and team A gets throw-in (or FTs if bonus) for B2’s foul on A2.

subPoints.heading: Definition
subPoints.body: Illegal contact with an opponent (holding, blocking, pushing, charging, tripping, bending into abnormal position outside cylinder) whether ball is live or dead.

subPoints.heading: Throw-in foul
subPoints.body: Personal foul committed when game clock <= 2:00 in Q4 or OT by a defensive player on an opponent on the court while the ball is out-of-bounds and at the thrower-in’s disposal.

subPoints.heading: Penalties
subPoints.body: Charged against offender:
bullets: 34.2.1 Not in act of shooting: throw-in nearest infraction (or 2 FTs if in team foul penalty).
34.2.2 In act of shooting: made basket counts + 1 FT; missed 2PT = 2 FTs; missed 3PT = 3 FTs.
34.2.3 Throw-in foul penalty: 1 FT (regardless of team fouls) + possession throw-in nearest infraction.

examples.text: Last 2:00 Q4/OT throw-in fouls: while ball at thrower’s disposal after OOB/foul (34-2), after made goal/FT behind endline (34-3 — no endline running after throw-in foul!), combined with technical foul (34-6), offensive throw-in foul (34-7), away from throw-in spot (34-8) vs AFTER ball leaves hands (34-9).
examples.interpretation: Before ball leaves thrower-in’s hands in <= 2:00 Q4/OT, defensive foul anywhere on court = 1 FT (no line-up) + throw-in nearest foul (34-2, 34-3, 34-8), unless Flagrant or DQ (34-5). Offensive foul before release = team control personal throw-in to defense (34-7). Once ball leaves hands = ordinary personal foul (34-9).

subPoints.heading: Definition & 4 conditions
subPoints.body: 2 opponents commit fouls on each other at approximately the same time: both player fouls, both involve physical contact, between same 2 opponents, and either both personal or any combination of disruptive/flagrant/disqualifying.

subPoints.heading: Penalty
subPoints.body: Foul charged to each offender; NO free throws. Resume by scoring throw-in, team control throw-in nearest infraction, or jump ball situation if neither had control/entitlement.

examples.text: Technical fouls (35-2), unequal team foul counts (35-3), shooter fouls defender while shooting (35-4, 35-5), rebound/post pushing (35-6), mixed types: personal foul + flagrant foul at same time (35-7, 35-8, 35-9), and disruptive + flagrant/DQ combinations (35-10).
examples.interpretation: Only same-type fouls (2 personals OR any mix of DI/FL/DQ) form a double foul (35-10). Technical fouls never form double fouls. If personal + flagrant happen simultaneously, personal is ALWAYS treated as occurring FIRST and flagrant SECOND — they do NOT cancel (35-7, 35-8, 35-9).

articles.title: Technical foul
articles.subtitle: 2026 Two-Category System (Cat 1 counts toward GD; Cat 2 does NOT)

subPoints.heading: Rules of conduct & preventive warnings
subPoints.body: Demands full cooperation; referees may warn minor unintentional acts before calling a T. Late-recognised technical fouls still stop live play and administer as if occurring at the time charged (intervening play stays valid).

subPoints.heading: Category 1 vs. Category 2 technical fouls
subPoints.body: Divided into two severity categories:
bullets: Category 1 (COUNTS towards GD): Disrespectful communication/contact with officials/bench/opponents; offensive/inciting language or gestures; baiting/taunting/provoking (including minor contact); obstructing vision near eyes; excessive elbow swinging without contact; fake being fouled.

Category 2 (does NOT count towards GD): Delaying game (touching ball after basket, preventing prompt throw-in/FT, late to start game/2nd half); hanging on rim (beyond momentary dunk recovery or injury prevention); defensive goaltending on last free throw (1 pt + Cat 2 Tech).

subPoints.heading: Bench technical fouls & GD thresholds
subPoints.body: Bench technical fouls are Category 1 (charged to head coach C, B, or BD). Player DQ = 2 Cat 1 techs, OR 2 flagrants, OR 1 Cat 1 tech + 1 flagrant. Head coach DQ = 2 Cat 1 (C) OR 3 Cat 1 (B/BD/C). No extra FT for the DQ itself (36.2.5).

subPoints.heading: Penalty
subPoints.body: Player tech counts toward team fouls; bench tech does not. Opponents receive 1 immediate free throw (even if other penalties exist), then game resumes from point of interruption / team entitled before stoppage.

examples.text: Category 1 Technical Fouls (player behavioural non-contact or minor contact fouls + all bench personnel technicals) COUNT towards game disqualification (GD).
Game disqualification mix-and-match: Cat 2 T + Cat 1 T (36-3, 36-5) vs Cat 1 T + Flagrant (36-4).
examples.interpretation: Cat 2 T + Cat 1 T = NOT disqualified (only Cat 1 counts). 1 Cat 1 T + 1 Flagrant = DISQUALIFIED (36-4).

examples.text: Substitute A6 and assistant coach each get a bench technical, then another bench person gets a Cat 1 T.
examples.interpretation: Head coach accumulates 3 B/BD Cat 1 technicals -> Head Coach is disqualified (none count as team fouls).

examples.text: Delay-of-game warning applies to whole team (36-8); disconcerting shooter (waving near eyes, shouting, stomping) when shot is (a) made vs (b) missed (36-10).
examples.interpretation: If made (36-10a): warning (Cat 1 T if already warned). If missed (36-10b): immediate Cat 1 Technical Foul (shooter was disadvantaged).

examples.text: Illegal participation: 6 players on court (36-12, 36-13) or 5-foul excluded player back on court (36-15, 36-16, 36-17).
examples.interpretation: Correct immediately without disadvantaging opponents; points/fouls before detection remain valid; remove illegal/excluded player and charge head coach Cat 1 Tech (B1). Extra foul by excluded player goes on scoresheet after 5th foul AND B1 against coach (36-16b).

examples.text: Fake being fouled (flop) procedure: verbal/visual warning signal vs immediate Cat 1 T; head-snap during offensive foul (36-19), defensive foul (36-20), 2nd fake in same live play before stoppage (36-21), simultaneous double fake (36-22).
examples.interpretation: Each team gets 1 warning (signalled immediately without stopping play); 2nd fake by ANY teammate draws Cat 1 Tech even if clock never stopped to relay 1st warning (36-21a). Extreme no-contact fake can draw immediate Cat 1 T.

examples.text: Excessive swinging of elbows without contact (36-24); 2 Cat 1 T GD (36-26); 1 Cat 2 rim-hang + 1 Cat 1 T -> NOT DQ (36-27).
examples.interpretation: Swinging elbows without contact = Cat 1 Tech (36-24). Player hits GD at 2 Cat 1 T, 2 FL, or 1 Cat 1 T + 1 FL (timer must raise GD marker immediately, 36-26).

examples.text: Excluded 5-foul player committing Cat 1 Tech (36-29), DQ foul (36-30, 36-31), pushing opponent while going to bench (36-35, 36-37), or verbally abusing referee (36-36).
examples.interpretation: Any subsequent T by excluded player = B1 against head coach; subsequent DQ = D on player + B2 on head coach (36-30, 36-31). Players may stay on bench as excluded players (only DQ’d leave).

examples.text: Player head coach GD combinations: player Cat 1 T + bench B1 (36-39 = NOT DQ), player Cat 1 T + personal coach C1 (36-40 = GD), player FL + 2 bench B1 (36-41 = GD), coach C1 + player FL2 (36-42 = GD), interval fouls (36-44), 4 player fouls + 1 coach C1 = excluded as player (36-45).
examples.interpretation: All player Cat 1 T / FL fouls plus coach C1 and B/BD bench technicals count toward a player head coach’s disqualification and 5-foul exclusion limit (36-38, 36-45).

examples.text: Throw-in boundary crossing warnings & Cat 2 Tech (36-46–36-49); immediate 1 FT administration (36-50–36-55); Cat 1 Tech during shot in air vs ball in hands (36-56, 36-57).
examples.interpretation: Technical FT is shot immediately with no line-up (unless time-out requested, which runs BEFORE tech FT, 36-54). When shooter has ball in hands and teammate/coach A commits Cat 1 T, basket is cancelled (36-57b); if ball is in air, basket still counts (36-56b).

articles.title: Disruptive foul
articles.subtitle: 2026 Update — Replaced former Unsportsmanlike C3/C4/C5 transition & clock fouls; does NOT count toward GD

subPoints.heading: Definition
subPoints.body: Illegal player contact with an opponent which does not rise to the level of a flagrant foul, disrupts the flow of the game, and places the opponent at a disadvantage.

subPoints.heading: Criteria for disruptive fouls
subPoints.body: Awarded when a player commits any of the following three criteria:
bullets: An unnecessary contact caused by the defensive player, not legitimately attempting to directly play the ball, to stop the progress of the offensive team in transition (applies until the offensive player starts the act of shooting).

An unnecessary contact caused by the defensive player anywhere on the court, not legitimately attempting to directly play the ball, to stop the game clock and/or shot clock at the end of a quarter or overtime.

An illegal contact caused by a player from behind or laterally on an opponent who is progressing towards the opponent’s basket with NO opponents between the progressing player and the basket, and the player has ball control, is attempting to gain control, or a pass has been released to them (applies until act of shooting starts).

subPoints.heading: Consistency of interpretation
subPoints.body: The referee must interpret disruptive fouls consistently throughout the game and judge only the action.

subPoints.heading: Penalty (Overview)
subPoints.body: Entered on scoresheet as DI. Does NOT count towards 2-foul game disqualification (GD).

subPoints.heading: Player & team foul charge
subPoints.body: A disruptive foul shall be charged against the offender and shall count as one of the team fouls.

subPoints.heading: Free throws & frontcourt possession
subPoints.body: Free throw(s) awarded to the fouled player, followed by a throw-in from the throw-in line in the team’s frontcourt opposite the scorer’s table (with 14 s shot clock):
bullets: Not in act of shooting: 2 free throws + throw-in at frontcourt line.
In act of shooting, goal made: goal counts + 1 free throw + throw-in at frontcourt line.
In act of shooting, goal missed: 2 or 3 free throws + throw-in at frontcourt line.

examples.text: A disruptive foul is a player’s illegal contact which does not rise to a flagrant foul, disrupts the flow of the game and places opponent at a disadvantage: (1) unnecessary non-ball transition foul before act of shooting; (2) unnecessary non-ball foul anywhere to stop game/shot clock at end of quarter/OT; (3) illegal behind/lateral contact on progressing opponent with no defender ahead (has ball, attempting to gain, or pass released) before act of shooting. Does NOT count towards GD.
Team A starts a fast break. B1, not legitimately attempting to directly play the ball, grabs A1’s arm to stop team A’s transition before A1 starts the act of shooting.
examples.interpretation: B1 shall be charged with a disruptive foul. The contact is unnecessary, stops the progress of the offensive team in transition and occurs before the act of shooting starts.

examples.text: Team A gains control and starts a transition. B1 reaches across A1’s body and grabs A1’s shirt from the side without attempting to directly play the ball before A1 starts the act of shooting.
examples.interpretation: B1 shall be charged with a disruptive foul. The contact is unnecessary, is not a legitimate attempt to directly play the ball, stops the progress of offensive team in transition and occurs before the act of shooting starts.

examples.text: A1 is in transition and has started the act of shooting. B1 then makes unnecessary contact without attempting to directly play the ball.
examples.interpretation: The transition disruptive foul criteria no longer apply once the offensive player has started the act of shooting. The contact shall be judged by a referee according to the relevant personal or flagrant foul criteria, depending on the nature of the action and the severity of the contact.

examples.text: B1 reaches for the ball during team A’s transition and makes illegal contact on A1’s forearm while directly attempting to play the ball.
examples.interpretation: B1 shall not be charged with a disruptive foul solely because the contact occurs in transition. If the contact does not meet disruptive or flagrant criteria, it shall be penalised as a personal foul.

examples.text: With 30 seconds remaining in the fourth quarter, A1 catches the ball from A2’s throw-in. B1 wraps both arms around A1 at mid-court to stop the game clock. B1 is not attempting to play the ball.
examples.interpretation: If the contact does not rise to the level of a flagrant foul, B1 shall be charged with a disruptive foul. The contact is unnecessary, occurs near the end of the fourth quarter, and is committed to stop the game clock without a legitimate attempt to directly play the ball.

examples.text: With 18 seconds remaining in overtime, B1 deliberately pushes dribbler A1 in the back anywhere on the court, not legitimately attempting to play the ball.
examples.interpretation: If the contact does not rise to the level of a flagrant foul, B1 shall be charged with a disruptive foul. The contact is unnecessary, occurs near the end of the overtime, and is committed to stop the game clock without a legitimate attempt to directly play the ball.

examples.text: With 10 seconds remaining in Q4 (team B at 3 team fouls), A1 catches the ball and starts a moving shot. During A1’s upward motion, B1 pulls A1’s shirt from behind, not attempting to play the ball.
examples.interpretation: Contact occurred during act of shooting. If not flagrant, B1 is charged with a disruptive foul (to stop clock without playing ball): (a) If shot made -> goal counts + 1 FT + frontcourt throw-in line (14s). (b) If missed -> 2 or 3 FTs + frontcourt throw-in line (14s).

examples.text: A1 dribbles to the basket on a fast break and there is no opponent player between A1 and the opponents’ basket. B1 contacts A1 illegally from behind and a foul against B1 is called.
examples.interpretation: This is a disruptive foul by B1.

examples.text: While A1 is finishing a fast break and before A1 has gathered the ball in the hands to start the act of shooting, B1 contacts A1’s arm from behind trying to steal the ball. There is no opponent player between A1 and the opponent’s basket.
examples.interpretation: This is a disruptive foul by B1.

examples.text: While A1 is finishing a fast break at the free-throw line in team A’s frontcourt, and AFTER A1 has gathered the ball in the hands to start the act of shooting, B1 contacts A1’s arm from behind while attempting to tap the ball away. No opponent ahead.
examples.interpretation: The contact occurs after the act of shooting has started. Therefore, it does not meet the criteria for a disruptive foul. If B1’s contact does not meet the criteria for a flagrant foul, it shall be penalised as a personal foul.

examples.text: A1 passes from backcourt to A2 progressing towards opponents’ basket in frontcourt with no team B player between A2 and basket. A2 jumps and, before catching the ball, B1 fouls A2 from behind.
examples.interpretation: This is a disruptive foul by B1 for illegal contact on a progressing player from behind with no team B player between A2 and the basket.

examples.text: B1, in team B’s backcourt, taps the ball away from dribbler A1 and attempts to gain control of the ball. With no team A player between B1 and team A’s basket, A2 contacts B1 from behind or laterally.
examples.interpretation: This is a disruptive foul by A2. The illegal contact was from behind or laterally on a player progressing towards the basket with no opponent between the player and the basket.

examples.text: A1 has the ball in backcourt; A2 is progressing in frontcourt with no defender ahead. BEFORE A1 releases the pass to A2, B1 fouls A2 from behind.
examples.interpretation: The foul does not meet the criteria for a disruptive foul, as A1 has NOT yet released the ball on a pass to A2. Penalised as a personal foul, unless it rises to a flagrant foul.

articles.title: Flagrant foul
articles.subtitle: 2026 Update — Replaced C1/C2 Unsportsmanlike fouls; 2 Flagants or 1 Flagrant + 1 Cat 1 Tech = GD

subPoints.heading: Definition (38.1.1 – 38.1.2)
subPoints.body: Illegal contact violating sportsmanship/fair play whose nature or severity exceeds a personal or disruptive foul (judge only the action):
bullets: Not a legitimate basketball play against an opponent, with or without the ball.
Reckless, violent or dangerous act which causes or may cause injury to an opponent.
Excessive, hard contact in an effort to play the ball or an opponent.

subPoints.heading: Penalty — Free throws & possession
subPoints.body: Charged against offender (FL) and counts as team foul. 2 FTs (non-shooting) or made + 1 / missed 2–3 FTs (shooting), followed by throw-in from frontcourt throw-in line opposite scorer’s table (or Q1 jump ball if before start of play).

subPoints.heading: Game disqualification (GD)
subPoints.body: Player is disqualified for remainder of game upon 2 flagrant fouls, OR 2 category 1 technical fouls, OR 1 category 1 technical + 1 flagrant foul. No additional penalty is added for the GD itself.

examples.text: A flagrant foul is a player’s illegal contact violating sportsmanship and fair play exceeding personal or disruptive foul limits: (1) Not a legitimate basketball play against an opponent (with or without ball); (2) Reckless, violent or dangerous act causing or risking injury; (3) Excessive, hard contact in an effort to play the ball or opponent. Counts towards game disqualification.
A1 is dribbling near the sideline. B1 makes no legitimate basketball play and strikes A1 with excessive hard contact.
examples.interpretation: B1 shall be charged with a flagrant foul. The contact is not a legitimate basketball play and exceeds the limits of a personal foul.

examples.text: A1 is airborne on a 3-point shot attempt. B1 makes a reckless close-out and steps inside A1’s cylinder. After the release of the ball, A1 lands on B1’s foot and twists the ankle or otherwise becomes injured because of B1’s contact.
examples.interpretation: B1 shall be charged with a flagrant foul for reckless and dangerous play.

examples.text: A1 is airborne on a dunk attempt. B1 moves under A1, causing A1 to lose balance and land heavily on the floor.
examples.interpretation: B1 shall be charged with a flagrant foul for reckless and dangerous play.

examples.text: After A1’s unsuccessful shot for goal, B1 rebounds the ball and is immediately fouled by A2, who pulls B1’s arm. B1 reacts by swinging the elbows and making hard contact with A2’s chest.
examples.interpretation: A2 shall be charged with a personal foul, and B1 shall be charged with a flagrant foul for violent and dangerous play.

examples.text: A1 is airborne on a lay-up. B1 makes excessive, hard contact on A1 by pulling A1’s shoulders while attempting to stop the play.
examples.interpretation: B1 shall be charged with a flagrant foul, as the contact is excessive and exceeds the limits of a personal foul.

examples.text: A1 is driving into the restricted area. After A1 has gathered the ball and started the shooting motion towards the basket, B1 swings the arm while trying to deflect the ball and makes hard contact on A1’s arm, either by pulling down or by following through.
examples.interpretation: B1 shall be charged with a flagrant foul, as the contact is excessive and exceeds the limits of a personal foul.

subPoints.heading: Definition & coach replacement
subPoints.body: Any flagrant unsportsmanlike action by players, substitutes, coaches or delegation members. Disqualified head coach is replaced by first assistant coach, or captain if none.

subPoints.heading: Violence, public order & damaging equipment
subPoints.body: Violence must be stopped immediately and reported by crew chief. Repeating physical actions risking equipment damage after a coach warning leads to a technical or disqualifying foul.

subPoints.heading: Penalty (D) & dressing room rule
subPoints.body: Offender must go to dressing room or leave building. 2 FTs (non-contact/head coach) or shooting/non-shooting FTs (contact) + frontcourt throw-in line opposite scorer’s table. DQ of assistant/sub/excluded/delegation member is charged as B2/BD2 against head coach (unless active fight, where each gets 2 FTs).

examples.text: Post-whistle aggressive elbow to neck (39-2) or headbutt to face (39-3).
examples.interpretation: B1 disqualified (D2): 2 FTs (no line-up) for A1 + team A frontcourt throw-in line opposite scorer’s table (14s).

examples.text: Already disqualified A1 verbally abuses referee leaving court (39-5); frustrated A1 after travelling verbally abuses referee (39-7).
examples.interpretation: Already disqualified offender cannot be penalised again — report to competition body (39-5). Active player DQ’d for verbal abuse gets D2 -> 2 FTs any opponent + frontcourt throw-in opposite table (39-7).

examples.text: 5th foul + immediate DQ while walking to bench (39-9); punching teammate A2, punching spectator, sub A6 punching A7, or damaging shot clock (39-11); additional flagrant/DQ act walking to locker room (39-13).
examples.interpretation: 5th foul excluded player DQ’d = D on player + B2 on head coach (39-9). DQ covers violence against teammates, spectators, and equipment (39-11). Additional acts en route to dressing room are reported only (39-13).

subPoints.heading: Leaving the team bench area (40.2.1 – 40.2.3)
subPoints.body: Applies to substitutes, coaches, excluded players, and delegation members leaving bench during a fight or situation that may lead to one. All bench personnel leaving are disqualified EXCEPT head coach / first assistant coach strictly assisting referees to restore order.

subPoints.heading: Penalty
subPoints.body: Regardless of how many leave bench, a single technical foul (B) is charged to head coach (disqualifications do NOT count as team fouls). Active involvement in fight incurs individual 2-FT disqualifying fouls under 39.3.4.

examples.text: Team A has possession 20s vs 5s when fight looms; 2 substitutes from EACH team leave bench (40-2).
examples.interpretation: Substitutes DQ’d (D + F spaces); equal B2/B2 penalties cancel; team A resumes throw-in nearest ball with remaining shot clock (4s or 19s).

examples.text: A6 leaves bench (40-4); A1 & B1 fight + A6 & B6 enter peacefully + A7 enters & punches B1 (40-5); A6 & manager enter & fight actively (40-6); coach pushes B1 (40-7); time-out players on court near bench (40-8).
examples.interpretation: Leaving bench without active fighting charges SINGLE B2 on coach (cancels if both teams, 40-5). Active fighting by sub = D2 (2 FTs), by manager = BD2 (2 FTs, doesn’t count to coach GD) -> 6 FTs total in 40-6. Head coach receives ONE D2 only even if also fighting (40-7). Players legitimately near bench on timeout stay immune unless leaving bench vicinity to fight (40-8).

articles.title: Foul limits by a player/head coach and game disqualifications

subPoints.heading: 5-foul limit & excluded player foul
subPoints.body: At 5 fouls a player must leave immediately. Player head coach with 5 player fouls becomes an excluded player but may keep coaching (41.2). A foul by a previously excluded player counts as B against the head coach (41.3).

subPoints.heading: Game disqualification (GD) & 30-second exit
subPoints.body: Timer raises GD marker when player hits 2 Cat 1 techs / 2 flagrants / 1+1, or head coach hits 2 C / 3 total bench techs. Disqualified person has max 30 s to leave to dressing room or leave building.

examples.text: Player A1 receives a Category 1 Technical Foul in Q1 and a Flagrant Foul (or second Cat 1 Technical Foul) in Q3.
examples.interpretation: Timer immediately raises the GD marker and notifies a referee; A1 is game disqualified and must go to dressing room or leave building within 30 seconds.

subPoints.heading: 4 team fouls threshold
subPoints.body: Personal, technical, disruptive, flagrant, and disqualifying fouls by a player count as team fouls. Team enters penalty after its 4th team foul in a quarter. Interval fouls count in next quarter/OT; OT fouls stay in Q4 count.

subPoints.heading: Penalty administration
subPoints.body: Subsequent defensive non-shooting personal fouls award 2 FTs to fouled player. Personal fouls by team in control / entitled to ball always award a throw-in, never bonus FTs.

examples.text: Team B has 4 team fouls in Q2. During the Q2–Q3 interval, B1 commits a Category 1 technical foul (42.1.2), OR A1 commits a 5th team-A offensive control foul against B1 (42.2.2).
examples.interpretation: Interval fouls count toward Q3 team fouls (not Q2). Personal fouls by the team in control (offensive fouls) ALWAYS result in a throw-in for opponents, never 2 bonus free throws.

subPoints.heading: Multiple fouls in same dead-ball period
subPoints.body: List fouls in chronological order; cancel equal/double penalties in order; always administer any technical foul first (except coach B/BD for bench DQ); last penalty possession cancels prior possession rights; if all equal penalties cancel out, resume by goal, prior control throw-in, or jump ball.

examples.text: B1 flagrant vs shooter + shot-clock horn (43-2); double foul on shooter by B1 then B2 (43-3); DI/FL followed by both coaches Ts (43-4); personal foul on made shot + shooter T (43-5, 43-6) vs flagrant on made shot + shooter T (43-7).
examples.interpretation: Flagrant before shot-clock violation stays valid and wipes violation if missed (43-2a). Equal team penalties cancel in order; unequal FL + T do NOT cancel (43-7).

examples.text: B1 fouls A1 -> A1 throws ball at B1’s body (43-8 = T) vs face (43-9 = D2); B1 foul + B2 tech (43-10); B1 DI/FL + A2/B2 Tech (43-11).
examples.interpretation: Always administer technical foul 1 FT FIRST (43-10, 43-11) UNLESS subsequent DQ cancels prior throw-in right (43-9a). Team-B foul + T shoots T first, then A1 FTs/throw-in (43-10).

examples.text: Equal/double fouls during FT activity (43-13); bench-DQ B2 exception (43-14, 43-15 = NOT administered first!); interval equal DQ/T cancellation (43-17); foul BEFORE vs AFTER ball becomes live on throw-in (43-18).
examples.interpretation: Equal fouls during FTs are recorded but penalties NOT administered (43-13). Coach B2 from fighting sub disqualification runs AFTER earlier personal FTs in chronological order (43-15). Once throw-in ball becomes live at disposal, prior throw-in penalty cannot be cancelled (43-18b).

subPoints.heading: Shooter designation
subPoints.body: Contact fouls: fouled player shoots (before any substitution, or by sub/coach-picked teammate if injured/5-fouled/DQ). Tech or non-contact DQ: head coach designates any opponent.

subPoints.heading: 5-second shot & rebounding lane restrictions
subPoints.body: Shooter has 5 s behind FT line, may not fake or cross line before ring/make. Lane players (alternating 1 m slots) may not enter lane/neutral zone/leave before ball leaves hand; outside players stay behind 3PT & FT line extended until ball touches ring/enters.

subPoints.heading: Violation penalties
subPoints.body: Shooter violation on made FT cancels point. Non-shooter violation on made FT is disregarded (point counts). On missed last FT: shooter/teammate violation = opponents’ FT-line-extended throw-in; opponent violation = substitute FT; both teams = jump ball.

examples.text: Empty rebound lane spaces (44-2); B2 enters lane early AND A1 misses FT cleanly or violates simultaneously on last FT (44-4).
examples.interpretation: Opponents need not fill lane slots, remaining behind FT extended & 3PT line (44-2). Simultaneous FT violation by both teams on missed last FT = jump ball situation (44-4).

subPoints.heading: General procedures (45.1.1 – 45.1.3)
subPoints.body: Referees may stop game immediately upon spotting an error unless disadvantaging either team. Play/fouls/time between error and correction remain valid.

subPoints.heading: Category 1 errors & correction deadlines
subPoints.body: Includes unmerited/omitted FTs, wrong FT shooter, erroneous points, wrong player/coach foul/timeout recording, and game clock errors. Before 2:00 Q4 must be fixed before 2:00 Q4 (or first stoppage if crossed); after 2:00 Q4/OT must be fixed before ball becomes live after first stoppage; cannot fix after game-ending dead ball unless occurring after last stoppage.

subPoints.heading: Category 1 special procedures
subPoints.body: Specific remedies for unmerited FTs (cancel & resume), omitted FTs (disregarded if same team scored after wrong possession), wrong shooter (cancel & replace or turn over), point/scoresheet/clock corrections.

subPoints.heading: Category 2 errors — Shot clock
subPoints.body: Covers shot clock starting/stopping/setting errors. Correctable on live-ball immediate stop or first stoppage while original team retains control/entitlement; NO LONGER correctable after change of live-ball possession, valid score by team in control, or end of game (45.6.2).

examples.text: Correctable Error Category 1 timelines (45-1–45-5): before 2:00 Q4 must be caught before 2:00 Q4 (45-3); after 2:00 Q4/OT must be caught before ball becomes live after FIRST stoppage (45-4, 45-5).
examples.interpretation: If first stoppage passes with <= 2:00 Q4 and ball goes live again, Category 1 error expires (45-4b, 45-5c/d).

examples.text: Unmerited FTs cancelled & FT-line ext if clock didn’t start (45-7); omitted FTs lost once same team scores after wrong throw-in (45-9c, 45-10), otherwise re-enter benched A1 to shoot (45-12); wrong shooter permitted vs referee directed wrong shooter (45-14–45-18).
examples.interpretation: Permitting wrong shooter cancels FTs -> turn over at FT line ext (or spot stopped if clock ran, 45-14, 45-15). Referee DIRECTING wrong shooter cancels wrong shots and lets correct player re-shoot (45-17, 45-18).

examples.text: Wrongly awarded/cancelled points (45-20, 45-21); foul reported on wrong player/team B2 vs B1 (45-23); scorer’s timeout/technical error (45-25, 45-26); game-clock malfunction or wrong set time 1:43 -> 2:43 caught in Q1, half-time, Q3-Q4 interval, Q4 > 2:00 vs <= 2:00 (45-28, 45-29).
examples.interpretation: Scoresheet/wrong-player/score/clock errors are correctable before 2:00 Q4: e.g., missed 1:00 of Q2 caught at half-time -> play 1:00 same direction before starting Q3 (45-29b); caught before Q4 -> play 11-min Q4 (45-29c).

examples.text: Category 2 Shot Clock errors: sudden 24s reset (45-31); frontcourt set 24s instead of 14s (45-32); backcourt set 14s instead of 24s (45-33, 45-34) vs expired after possession change or same-team score (45-35).
examples.interpretation: Shot clock errors are fixed at exact remaining time (16s, 4s, 10s) as long as same team stays in control, BEFORE change of live-ball possession or a made goal by team in control (45-35).

title: Referees, Table Officials, Commissioner: Duties and Powers

subPoints.heading: Crew structure, neutrality & uniform
subPoints.body: Crew chief + 1 or 2 umpires; 4 table officials (scorer, assistant scorer, timer, shot clock operator) + optional commissioner sitting between scorer and timer. Have no authority to change rules.

examples.text: During an unexpected clock stoppage, table officials notice an irregularity while the commissioner is seated between the scorer and timer.
examples.interpretation: Commissioner supervises table officials and assists the crew chief, but officials must apply the Official Rules strictly with no authority to alter them.

subPoints.heading: Inspection, clocks, ball & stoppages
subPoints.body: Approves equipment, designates official clocks, picks game ball from >= 2 home balls, removes dangerous objects, starts Q1 jump ball, may stop/forfeit game.

subPoints.heading: Jurisdiction (20 min pre-game to signature), reports & final decisions
subPoints.body: Authority spans 20 min before tip-off until game-ending horn approved; inspects & signs scoresheet (recording forfeits, DQs, pre/post-game unsportsmanlike acts on reverse). Resolves referee disagreements; handles IRS (App. F) and uncovered situations (47.14).

examples.text: Ten minutes after the final buzzer (while referees are in dressing room before signing the scoresheet), Player A5 commits unsportsmanlike behaviour in the tunnel; or two umpires disagree on an out-of-bounds call.
examples.interpretation: Crew chief’s jurisdiction lasts until signing the scoresheet (starts 20 min pre-game). Pre/post-game unsportsmanlike acts are entered on the reverse side and reported in writing. Crew chief makes the final decision on referee disagreements.

subPoints.heading: Jurisdiction, whistle discipline & officiating principles
subPoints.body: Jurisdiction extends inside/outside lines (table/bench areas). Do NOT whistle on made goals/FTs or when ball goes live. Apply spirit/intent, advantage/disadvantage, common sense, and game-control balance.

subPoints.heading: Protests, injured referee & finality
subPoints.body: 5-minute window before resuming without/replacing an injured referee; English required for clarifying international decisions; decisions are final unless protestable under Appendix C.

examples.text: Two post players briefly touch hand-to-hand away from the ball with neither gaining advantage nor restricting movement.
examples.interpretation: Under Art. 48.3 (advantage/disadvantage & balance), referees do not whistle incidental contact that gives no advantage and places neither player at a disadvantage.

subPoints.heading: Scoresheet, scoreboard & challenge tracking
subPoints.body: Scorer records rosters, points, player/coach fouls (notifying immediately on 5 fouls, coach/player GD, exhausted timeouts, or erroneous 2nd Head Coach’s Challenge), operates AP arrow (reverses at half-time). Assistant runs scoreboard; scoresheet prevails in unresolved discrepancies (49.2).

examples.text: Scoreboard displays 74–72 while official running score on scoresheet shows 75–72; or a head coach requests a second Head Coach’s Challenge after already using one.
examples.interpretation: Scorer notifies referee immediately on 2nd HCC request (refused). For scoreboard discrepancies that cannot be resolved, the official scoresheet takes precedence and scoreboard is corrected (49.2).

subPoints.heading: Game clock, foul markers, timeouts & intervals
subPoints.body: Measures playing time, timeouts (signals at 50 s & 60 s), and intervals (notifies at 3 min / 1.5 min before Q1/Q3, signals 30 s before Q2/Q4/OT). Stops game clock on horn, whistle, timeout against scoring goal, and every made goal when <= 2:00 in Q4/OT. Raises 1–5 / GD markers and red team-foul block after 4th foul.

examples.text: In Q4 with 1:40 left, Team A scores a basket (no foul/violation). Earlier in Q3, Team B reached its 4th team foul.
examples.interpretation: Timer immediately stops the game clock upon the made basket whenever <= 2:00 remains in Q4 or OT (50.2). Team foul marker turns completely RED with no number once live play resumes after the 4th team foul (50.1).

subPoints.heading: 24 s / 14 s / off states
subPoints.body: Controls 24s/14s device in sync with Art. 29:
bullets: 51.1 Start/Restart: live-ball control on court or throw-in legal touch (deflections do not reset).
51.2 Stop without reset: same-team OOB, injury, team T, JB (unless lodged), double foul, equal cancellation, or frontcourt stoppage with >= 14 s.
51.3 Reset 24 s (no display): made basket, defensive rebound off ring, backcourt throw-in for defense/JB/unrelated interruption, or free throws.

51.4 Reset 14 s (visible): same-team frontcourt stoppage with <= 13 s; new-team frontcourt throw-in; DI/FL/DQ frontcourt throw-in line; offensive rebound off ring; <= 2:00 frontcourt advancement with >= 14 s.
51.5 Switch off: new ball control after dead ball with < 14 s left on game clock.

examples.text: All Shot Clock OBRI cases (29/51-1 through 29/51-57) govern the Shot Clock Operator’s exact resets (24s / 14s / No Display) alongside Article 29.

title: Signals, Scoresheet, Protests, Classification, Media Time-outs & IRS

subPoints.heading: Standard hand signals & English verbal support
subPoints.body: Only illustrated FIBA hand signals (1–72) are valid: clock/scoring (1–6), subs/timeouts/informative (7–16), violations (17–26), player numbers 0–99 (27–36), foul types (37–51), special fouls/warnings including Signal 54 Disruptive Foul, Signal 55 Flagrant Foul, Signal 59 Illegal Boundary Crossing (52–59), IRS & HCC (60–61), and FT reporting/administration (62–72).

examples.text: Reporting a Disruptive Foul (Signal 54: raised clenched fist followed by two fingers at face level) or Flagrant Foul (Signal 55: grasp wrist upward) to scorer’s table.
examples.interpretation: Referees use only the 72 official FIBA hand signals and support reports verbally (in English for international games).

subPoints.heading: Four-copy form, two-colour ink & pre-game entries
subPoints.body: White/blue/pink/yellow copies (or electronic). RED pen for Q1 & Q3; BLUE/BLACK pen for Q2, Q4 & all OTs. Unused time-out boxes crossed with two parallel lines.

subPoints.heading: 2026 Foul codes & Head Coach’s Challenge box
subPoints.body: Codes: P (personal), T in circle (Cat 1 player T), T (Cat 2 player T), C in circle (coach unsportsmanlike T), B/BD in circle (bench T), DI (disruptive foul), FL in circle (flagrant foul), D (disqualifying), F (fighting), GD (game disqualification). Running score, summing up, and 1 HCC box (Q/OT + min) recorded under team name (B.13).

examples.text: 7 Disqualifying foul scoresheet scenarios for leaving bench vs active fighting (Head coach, 1st assistant, both coaches, substitute, 2 subs + excluded player, 1 or 2 accompanying delegation members).
examples.interpretation: Shows exact D / D2 / B2 / BD2 / F circle entries and FT totals (2, 4, 6, or 8 FTs + possession).

examples.text: Head coach technical fouls combined with delegation member fight BD (B-2 cases 1–4).
examples.interpretation: BD does NOT count toward coach GD; coach hits GD only at 2 C-fouls or 3 B/BD/C (non-fight) technicals.

examples.text: Player head coach foul combinations on scoresheet (cases 1–4).
examples.interpretation: 1 Cat 1 T (player) + 1 B1 = NOT DQ (case 1); 1 FL2 + 2 B1 = GD (case 2); 1 Cat 1 T + 1 C1 = GD (case 3); 4 player fouls + 1 B1 = excluded as player (case 4).

subPoints.heading: Admissibility, deadlines & CHF 1,500 fee
subPoints.body: Limited to Art. 45 score/clock/shot-clock failure with verifiable evidence, forfeit/cancellation decisions, or eligibility violations. Captain alerts crew chief/commissioner <= 15 min & signs scoresheet; written reasons <= 1 hour; CHF 1,500 deposit; decided within 24 hours.

examples.text: Team A believes a correctable scorekeeping error under Art. 45 was ignored despite verifiable evidence and files a protest.
examples.interpretation: Captain alerts crew chief within 15 minutes and signs protest box; written reasons within 1 hour; CHF 1,500 deposit (forfeited if rejected); competent body decides within 24 hours.

subPoints.heading: Classification points & tie-breakers
subPoints.body: 2 pts win, 1 pt loss (including default), 0 pts forfeit. Tie-breakers: head-to-head record -> H2H point diff -> H2H points scored -> group point diff -> group points scored -> FIBA ranking/draw (restarted from step 1 if any team separates). Covers cross-group and home-and-away aggregate series.

examples.text: 7 Round-Robin Group Tie-Breaker Worked Examples (2-way, 3-way, 4-way, and 5-way ties using H2H W-L -> H2H diff -> H2H pts -> group diff -> restart rule).
examples.interpretation: Once any subgroup separates at a step (e.g. 1st C, 5th A in D.2.7), repeat all tie-breaker criteria from step 1 for remaining tied teams (B, D, E).

examples.text: Forfeit nullification in groups & phases (Team 4A / Team 2B twice forfeits), and Cross-Group Ranking (Best 2nd/3rd placed team after annulling 6th-placed games).
examples.interpretation: 2nd forfeit nullifies ALL games across all carried-over phases (D.5.1). Cross-group comparison annuls last-placed results in larger groups so teams compare equal game counts without altering within-group standings.

examples.text: Home-and-Away Aggregate Series Examples 1–6 (tied first game 80–80, tied second game 75–75, tied aggregate 160–160 forcing Game 2 OT).
examples.interpretation: No OT in Game 1 even if tied (D.7.3). No OT in Game 2 if aggregate differs even when Game 2 is tied (D.7.4). Game 2 plays OTs only when 80-minute aggregate score is tied (D.7.5, D.7.6).

subPoints.heading: Per-quarter TV break procedure
subPoints.body: Optional competition rule: 1 Media time-out per quarter (never in OT) of 60/75/90/100 s. If no team requests before <= 5:00 in quarter, granted uncharged at first dead-ball stoppage; if a team requested earlier, it serves as both team & media time-out.

examples.text: In a competition with 75-second Media Time-outs, neither team calls a timeout before 4:40 left in Q1; at 4:40 an out-of-bounds occurs.
examples.interpretation: Media Time-out (75s) is granted immediately at 4:40 and charged to NEITHER team (E.3.2). Had Team A called a timeout earlier at 6:10, it would have lasted 75s and counted as both Team A’s timeout and Q1’s Media Time-out (E.3.3).

articles.title: Instant Replay System & Head Coach’s Challenge (F.1 – F.4)

subPoints.heading: IRS authority & clear and conclusive evidence
subPoints.body: Authorised until crew chief signs scoresheet. Crew chief + at least 1 umpire (caller) review. Initial call can only be overturned with clear and conclusive visual evidence.

subPoints.heading: Reviewable situations
subPoints.body: Divided by timing window:
bullets: F.3.1 End of quarter/OT: buzzer-beater release, remaining clock on OOB/shot-clock/8s/foul.
F.3.2 <= 2:00 Q4/OT: shot clock release, off-ball foul timing/act of shooting, throw-in defensive foul (ball in hand/disposal), goaltending/interference, OOB identity.

F.3.3 Any time of game: 2/3-pt shot area, 2/3 FTs, goaltending after foul, upgrading/downgrading personal/disruptive/flagrant/DQ/technical fouls, Cat 1/Cat 2 correctable errors (Art. 45), clock malfunction, FT shooter identity, violence/bench involvement.

subPoints.heading: Head Coach’s Challenge (HCC)
subPoints.body: Each head coach gets 1 HCC per game regardless of outcome, usable at any time for any F.3 situation (time limits of F.3.1–F.3.2 do not restrict HCC). Coach makes visual contact, says "challenge" loudly in English, and draws rectangle with hands; signal 61 alerts scorer.

examples.text: IRS General Principles: non-approved team camera denied (F-1.2); end-quarter teams stay on court (F-2.2); delayed fast-break stop after 3PT uncertainty (F-2.4); cancelling TO/sub until IRS finishes (F-2.6, F-2.7).
examples.interpretation: Only crew-chief-approved IRS may be used. Teams stay on court at buzzer reviews. Requested timeouts/subs wait and can be withdrawn after IRS decision is announced.

examples.text: End-of-quarter/OT reviews: buzzer shot release (F-3.1.1), foul before OT horn (F-3.1.2, F-3.1.3), shooter OOB (F-3.1.4), prior shot-clock or 8s violation + remaining clock 0.6s / 3.4s (F-3.1.5, F-3.1.6) vs non-shooter OOB disallowed (F-3.1.7).
examples.interpretation: IRS can review shooter OOB, shot clock, 8s, or foul ONLY in connection with end-of-quarter/OT; cannot review non-shooting OOB (F-3.1.7).

examples.text: <= 2:00 Q4/OT reviews: shot-clock release (F-3.2.1), off-ball foul vs act of shooting & order (F-3.2.2–F-3.2.5; cannot review order of T vs FL, F-3.2.6), goaltending/interference reversal resumption & immediate clear control (F-3.2.7–F-3.2.18), OOB identity (F-3.2.19 vs F-3.2.20, F-3.2.21), and throw-in ball-in-hand foul check (F-3.2.22–F-3.2.24).
examples.interpretation: Goaltending/interference IRS applies ONLY when the referees have called a violation (F-3.2.17). Also IRS cannot review foul order (F-3.2.6) or non-shooter OOB (F-3.2.21).

examples.text: Any-time reviews: cannot check shooter act-of-shooting before foul (F-3.3.1); 2PT vs 3PT & 2/3 FT check (F-3.3.2–F-3.3.5); goaltending/interference after foul (F-3.3.6–F-3.3.15); upgrading/downgrading fouls vs no-contact non-cancellation (F-3.3.16–F-3.3.24); Cat 1/2 errors & clock malfunctions (F-3.3.25–F-3.3.32); acts of violence / altercations (F-3.3.33–F-3.3.44).
examples.interpretation: On foul upgrade/downgrade IRS, zero contact still CANNOT cancel a personal foul (F-3.3.19) or turn defense foul into charge (F-3.3.21), EXCEPT non-contact elbow swing changes FL to Cat 1 T (F-3.3.17). Uncalled violence review can retroactively add FL but loses possession if play continued (F-3.3.38–F-3.3.44).

examples.text: Head Coach’s Challenge (HCC) cases: withdrawing before referee grants (F-4.2); non-challengeable uncalled GT or travel (F-4.3, F-4.4) vs 8s Q2 non-buzzer (F-4.10); challenging 2PT/3PT late (F-4.5–F-4.8); OOB in Q2/Q4 (F-4.9, F-4.16); Cat 1 error HCC retention if clock expired violation (F-4.12); during timeout (F-4.14); upgrade to DI/FL (F-4.20 vs too late in F-4.21); head coach only (F-4.22).
examples.interpretation: 1 HCC per game regardless of outcome, usable at ANY game time for any F.3 situation, requested ONLY by head coach. Only granted HCCs go on scoresheet (F-4.23); must request before ball becomes live again at next stoppage (F-4.21).
